### Original 2026-08-17 investigation (preserved for the record)

User-reported: when a dog (or, it turns out, a hyena -- see below) pins the player down in Survival, requiring a melee/struggle-free prompt, the on-screen prompt gets no controller-glyph treatment like this project's other interact/gameplay hints already do -- completely overlooked until now, no prior investigation existed anywhere in this file or `iw5sp.md`.

**Real assets confirmed** (`D:\Tools\OpenAssetTools\zone_dump\`):
- `materials\hud_dog_melee.json` -> references image `hint_dog_melee` (`images\hint_dog_melee.dds`, confirmed 64x64 via its own DDS header, DXT-compressed).
- A SECOND, previously-unknown-to-this-project asset pair exists right next to it: `hud_hyena_melee.json` / `hint_hyena_melee` -- MW3 Survival has (at least) two animal enemy types with their own melee-struggle prompt icon, not just dogs.
- Both materials are referenced in `zone_source\common_survival.zone` (`image,hint_dog_melee` / `material,hud_dog_melee` / `image,hint_hyena_melee` / `material,hud_hyena_melee`, lines 2938-2941) -- **confirms this is genuinely Survival-relevant**, not Campaign-only, directly answering the scope question this investigation opened with.

**Why this is architecturally DIFFERENT from every other glyph-covered hint in this project, and why nothing was implemented this pass**: every hint this project's existing glyph pipeline covers (interact/reload/pickup/mantle prompts) is real LOCALIZED TEXT with a keyboard-key substring the bind-resolver hook (`FUN_0061f6f0`) intercepts and swaps a controller-glyph codepoint into. The dog/hyena melee HUD elements are NOT text -- they're pre-baked 2D icon MATERIALS (`techniqueSet: "2d"` in their own JSON). **Actually decoded the DDS pixel content this pass** (ffmpeg converts DDS->PNG directly, no external tool needed): both `hint_dog_melee.dds` and `hint_hyena_melee.dds` are plain 64x64 gray-on-transparent SILHOUETTES of the animal (a German Shepherd and a hyena respectively) -- **NOT a button/key icon at all, no keyboard key baked in**. This is almost certainly an enemy-identification graphic (e.g. "you're being attacked by X"), not the interactive escape-prompt itself.

**This means the actual "press E to escape" TEXT most likely exists as a SEPARATE, ordinary localized string** created by the same encounter logic, which may already flow through this project's EXISTING bind-resolver/hint-text glyph pipeline like every other interact prompt -- the real, narrower open question is whether it does, not whether a whole new icon-rendering system needs building. `zone_source\common_survival.zone` lists `scriptfile,1550` immediately after the two icon/material pairs (line 2942, before the German Shepherd's own xmodel/material assets) -- almost certainly the compiled GSC script driving this specific encounter (dog-pin/hyena-pin logic, likely creating both the silhouette HUD icon AND the escape-prompt text/hudelem together). Decompiling a compiled GSC scriptfile is out of scope for this pass (no GSC decompiler available in this environment) and wouldn't settle this alone anyway -- GSC would show WHICH string/hudelem call is used, not whether the ALREADY-EXISTING native bind-resolver hook actually intercepts it live.

**Searched for a hookable native function for the ICON specifically, found none** (kept for the record, now lower-priority given the icon likely doesn't need glyph treatment at all): grepped `iw5sp.exe` directly (`grep -a`) for `hud_dog_melee`/`hint_dog_melee`/`hud_hyena_melee`/`hint_hyena_melee`/`struggle` -- zero matches; the material names aren't hardcoded ASCII anywhere in the executable, consistent with script-driven (not exe-hardcoded) HUD element creation.

**Deliberately NOT attempting a blind implementation this pass**: this project has a strong, repeatedly-demonstrated standard this exact session of never guessing a hook point or screen position without either (a) a confirmed, disassembly-verified function, or (b) live capture against the real game moment (every existing `kManualGlyphPositions` entry was calibrated this way, never automatically). A dog/hyena pin-down is a scripted, mid-combat Survival encounter with no known reliable way to trigger on demand outside real play -- there is no way to live-verify anything (whether the existing pipeline already covers the real text prompt, or where on screen it sits) this pass.

**Recommended next step, not yet done**: reach an actual dog/hyena pin-down in real Survival play with `HudGlyphPositionLogging`/`BindResolverHookLogging` enabled (both already exist, `[Experimental]` section, `mw3ncp_config.ini`) and check `proxy_d3d9.log` for whether the real escape-prompt text passes through the bind-resolver hook at all. If it does: this is likely a small, ordinary `kManualGlyphPositions` calibration addition, same as every other hint gap this project has closed. If it doesn't (a genuinely separate string-resolution path): further RE is needed, scoped much smaller now that the icon itself is confirmed out of scope.

## 79. Extended-session stutter -- three real, evidence-backed causes found and fixed; one residual (enemy-look GPU cost) PARKED, not resolved (2026-08-17/18)

**Status: Mostly fixed, live-confirmed "miles better."** One narrower residual symptom (visible dip specifically when looking toward enemies) remains open, explicitly parked rather than chased further this pass.

**Investigation timeline, each cause found via real evidence, not guessed:**
1. **`proxy_d3d9.log` opened in append ("a") mode**, never trimmed between launches -- a real install's log had grown to 2.6GB / 22.5 million lines across every session since install. Fixed: truncate ("w") mode, fresh log every launch.
2. **Background controller-poll thread continuously rescanned up to 4 XInput slots plus DualSense every ~4ms tick**, regardless of whether the active device had changed. Fixed: determines the active controller/slot ONCE at boot and locks onto it for the session -- steady-state cost drops to exactly one real read per tick. Switching to a different XInput slot or between XInput/DualSense now needs a relaunch to be picked up; the SAME device reconnecting (unplug/replug) does not.
3. **`HudGlyphPositionLogging`'s dedup compared only against the single most-recently-logged string**, not a real seen-set -- a normal HUD screen with multiple text elements re-logged almost every frame. One combat session produced 423,063 lines from this alone (91% of the entire log file) -- directly explained a live report of "stutter when we get shot or are approaching enemies" (exactly when HUD text churns fastest: hit markers, kill feed, ammo count). Fixed with a real 64-entry seen-set; this diagnostic defaults OFF regardless and is only ever meant for brief, targeted use.
4. **Co-op damage-rumble bug found along the way** (separate from the stutter itself, same investigation window): `PollDamageRumble` always read player-entity array index 0 ("SP is always player index 0" -- true for Campaign, not 2-player Survival co-op). A client player (not host) got rumble driven by their TEAMMATE's health. Mitigated: damage-rumble disables itself when a second real player entity is detected, rather than risk rumbling for the wrong player. Real fix (finding the actual "which index is THIS client" mechanism) needs further RE, not done this pass.

**A/B tested directly against v0.2.2** (rebuilt from the `v0.2.2` git tag in an isolated worktree, deployed for real side-by-side comparison, then restored) -- user-confirmed v0.2.2 "doesn't suffer anywhere near as bad," confirming the regression is real and mod-introduced (post-v0.2.2), not purely inherent engine behavior, though the user's own theory is both are true to some degree (MW3's real architectural/streaming limits as an old DX9-only engine, PLUS the mod's own added overhead on top).

A custom per-frame benchmark tool was built this pass specifically to catch cases like these directly: `FrametimeBenchmarkLogging` (`[Experimental]`, `mw3ncp_config.ini`) writes `frametime_benchmark.csv` (real per-frame timing via `QueryPerformanceCounter` at the same `Hook_EndScene` cadence RTSS itself uses) plus a breakdown of this project's own hook costs (options menu/overlay/glyph/hint draw time, rumble, asset-capture, real `CreateTexture` cost) so a felt stutter can be checked against real data instead of guessed -- this is how causes 1-3 above were actually found and confirmed, not theorized.

**PARKED, not resolved: a residual dip specifically when looking toward enemies** (user-reported "I saw about 20-30fps"). Checked directly against a real capture -- neither of the two biggest spikes in that session were combat-related (both were menu/level-load events, confirmed via direct `proxy_d3d9.log` correlation at the exact same moment), and no sustained elevated-frametime stretch exists anywhere in the data (longest run of frames over 10ms was 2 frames). Every one of this project's own instrumented hook costs stayed near-zero throughout. Leading theory, not yet confirmed: this may be **GPU-bound** rendering cost (enemy skeletal animation/shadows/lighting) rather than CPU-bound -- `Hook_EndScene`'s CPU-side timing wouldn't cleanly catch GPU backpressure, which can show up delayed/smeared across frames rather than as one clean spike tied to the exact moment an enemy comes into view. An MSI Afterburner/RTSS hardware-monitoring log was attempted as a cross-check but the one captured (`HardwareMonitoring.hml`) showed the GPU at 0-2% usage with `Framerate`/`Frametime` both `N/A` for the entire window -- RTSS wasn't actually hooked into the game process during that capture, so it didn't help this time. **Recommended next step, not yet done**: a real RTSS-hooked capture (confirm the in-game FPS overlay is actually visible before/during the test) correlated against a fresh `frametime_benchmark.csv`, or real GPU profiling (RenderDoc/PIX) if CPU-side correlation continues to come up empty.

**Real correlation found (2026-08-25, issue #87's own investigation)**: user directly tested and confirmed **"just res above 1080p... my guess is the engine supports it poorly"** -- 4:3 resolutions are fine, 1080p is fine, anything ABOVE 1080p (1440p specifically tested, described as "a mess") shows the stutter. A dedicated fork audit of this project's own resolution-scaling code (`GetResolutionScale`, `overlay_hud.cpp`) found no bug: 1440p is exactly 16:9 like 1080p (`scaleX == scaleY` at both, unlike the real, already-fixed non-16:9 distortion bug this project had before), already independently confirmed working correctly at 1440p in an earlier session (a real user report, font-tier fix), and no per-pixel loop or resolution-scaled render target exists anywhere in the normal gameplay draw path (every hint/icon texture is a fixed 512x64 atlas regardless of screen resolution; the only resolution-sized effect, the Options-screen blur, is gated behind a default-off preview feature). This strongly corroborates the GPU-bound theory above rather than a mod-side scaling bug -- this old engine's rendering pipeline was built and tuned for a console-era 1080p-and-below target, and a real GPU cost scaling poorly past that is a plausible, previously-unconfirmed native ceiling. **Still not proven by real GPU profiling** (RenderDoc/PIX, the same recommended-but-never-done next step above) -- this is a strong correlation, not a confirmed root cause, but the cleanest evidence yet that this specific residual is a genuine engine limitation, not something further changes to this mod's own code can fix.

## 80. Full save states (emulator-style) — PAUSED, KEY FEATURE (2026-08-25)

**Status: Paused, by explicit user request** ("how about we come back to this in future and disable for now"). Not started, no RE work done beyond the investigation below. Logged here so it isn't lost -- still explicitly a KEY mod feature, not a minor/debug-only convenience, just deliberately deprioritized for now rather than actively worked. Do not resume without the user raising it again.

**The ask (direct quotes, 2026-08-25):** "save states are something we lowk want" -- clarified immediately after when an earlier draft of this entry scoped it too narrowly to the F2 glyph-editor debug workflow: **"not for the editor, its a key mod feature. full save states like emulators."** This is emulator-style save-state functionality as a real, standalone, player-facing feature of the mod itself (save the exact current game state at any point during Campaign/Survival, reload it instantly, same category of feature as a Dolphin/RetroArch/PCSX2 save slot) -- not a debug tool, not scoped to calibration work, and not the same ask as the F2 debug-freeze feature it came up alongside.

**Why this is a real, separate project, not a quick add-on:** a genuine save-state needs to snapshot and later restore a large, currently-unmapped slice of live engine state -- player entity transform/health/inventory/weapon state, AI entity states, physics world state, script/GSC VM state (`level`/`self` struct fields, active threads/timers), and likely more depending on how much fidelity is wanted (a save that silently drops in-flight script timers or AI state would resume looking subtly wrong, not cleanly). None of this state has been mapped by this project's RE work so far -- everything found to date (dvars, kbuttons, per-player state flags, the pause/menu path) is comparatively narrow surface area next to a full entity/world/VM snapshot.

**Real tension with this project's own standing policy:** the top-level CLAUDE.md's permanently-removed aim-assist section establishes a hard-line rule against reading live gameplay-entity memory, based on real VAC/anti-cheat research (`re_notes/known_issues.md` issue #33) -- reasoned as SP/Survival-relevant too, not just MP-specific, since the policy itself was never scoped only to MP. A save-state feature is a fundamentally different shape of read (snapshotting entity/world state to serialize it, not reading it every frame to drive gameplay behavior like the removed aim-assist did) and this project's own single-player/Survival-only scope removes the VAC angle specifically (no VAC on `iw5sp.exe`) -- but it's still real entity-memory reading at a scale well beyond anything shipped so far, and deserves its own explicit go/no-go conversation rather than either assuming the aim-assist ban carries over uncritically or assuming it obviously doesn't apply.

**Before any implementation work starts, this needs:**
1. ~~A scoping conversation: full save-anywhere/reload-anywhere (hardest, most general), or a narrower first version~~ **Resolved 2026-08-25: user explicitly wants full cross-relaunch persistence ("must survive a relaunch from day one") — same-session-only was offered and declined.**
2. ~~Check whether the game already has ANY native save/checkpoint/quickload mechanism reachable via a console command or dvar first~~ **Checked 2026-08-25 -- see "Native save/load system found, but NOT reachable as a plain console command" below.**
3. The explicit risk discussion flagged above, specific to this feature (not inherited from the aim-assist decision) -- SP/Survival-only scope changes the calculus, but the decision should still be made deliberately, not assumed.
4. Real RE work to map the actual entity/world/script-VM structures that would need snapshotting, before any prototype is attempted.

**RULED OUT 2026-08-25: raw byte-for-byte process-memory dump/restore, even for cross-relaunch persistence specifically.** User's direct question ("cant we just dump and restore?") prompted a real empirical test rather than a guess, since it would have been a dramatically smaller lift than semantic struct mapping if it worked: a one-time diagnostic (`InstallEndSceneHook`, temporarily) logged `GetModuleHandleA(nullptr)` (exe base), `GetProcessHeap()`, and a fresh `HeapAlloc` test block's address on first device creation, compared across two genuinely separate launches (main menu only, no level load needed):
```
Launch 1: exeBase=00400000  processHeap=02A60000  testAlloc=0D61EAF8
Launch 2: exeBase=00400000  processHeap=02AF0000  testAlloc=0C997328
```
`exeBase` is identical both times, confirming what the PE-header check already showed (`iw5sp.exe` has `DYNAMIC_BASE`/ASLR disabled, always loads at `0x400000`) -- so the exe's own static/global data (a lot of what this project already hooks: dvars, per-player state structs, kbutton tables) IS stable across relaunches and safe for a raw dump/restore. But `processHeap` and `testAlloc` differ both times, by inconsistent deltas -- proof that Windows' own per-process **heap randomization** (a separate OS-level mitigation from the exe's own ASLR flag, and NOT controllable via anything in the exe itself) still applies to this process's default heap. A follow-up attempt to disable it specifically for `iw5sp.exe` via `Set-ProcessMitigation -Name iw5sp.exe -Disable BottomUp,HighEntropy` failed with `ACCESS_DENIED` (writes `HKLM\...\Image File Execution Options`, needs an elevated session) -- **user explicitly declined pursuing elevation, choosing to go semantic instead rather than fight an OS mitigation.** Bottom line: any dynamically (heap-)allocated game state -- almost certainly including entity arrays, AI state, and the GSC VM's own heap -- lands at a DIFFERENT address every separate launch, so a save captured in one process can never be blindly replayed into a freshly-launched one; the pointers inside it would all be dangling. Same-session-only saves (no relaunch between save and load) would NOT have hit this problem, since heap addresses are stable for the LIFE of one process -- this is specifically a cross-relaunch blocker, confirming the tradeoff flagged when that scope question was first asked.

**Native save/load system found, but NOT reachable as a plain console command (checked and closed out 2026-08-25).** A live PE string scan of `iw5sp.exe` turned up a real, apparently comprehensive native save/load system: `G_LoadGame`, `Savegame`, and genuine engine-level error-checking strings (`Corrupt Savegame - Expected sentinel sequence...`, `entitynum out of range`, `Invalid physics body count... Savegame is invalid`, `the bsp file has changed since the game was saved`, `savegame '%s' is wrong version`) -- this is a real serializer, not a shallow flag. Confirmed on disk: `players2/save/<levelname>.svg` (one per Campaign level, e.g. `london.svg`, `sp_dubai.svg`) plus numbered checkpoint files under `players2/save/autosave/` (e.g. `london-1.svg`) -- genuine, currently-in-use per-level autosave/checkpoint files. **No Survival-specific save/checkpoint string exists anywhere in the binary**, and the BSP-version error string strongly implies this system is tied to a loaded Campaign level identity -- consistent with the user's own upfront doubt ("it does but im not sure it will work how we want (campaign has)").

Two real command-shaped tokens exist in the strings (`save`, `loadgame`), and `Cmd_ExecuteString` is separately documented (this file, task #10 section above) as falling through to a real cvar-set check for unrecognized tokens -- so a plain `Cbuf_AddText(clientIndex, "save mw3ncp_test\n")` / `"loadgame mw3ncp_test\n"` was tried live (temporary F6/F7 test hotkeys, gated behind `glyphPositionEditMode`, using the same already-confirmed `Cbuf_AddText` path the F2 `timescale` freeze uses). **Result: negative.** `proxy_d3d9.log` confirmed both commands were genuinely submitted (`[savestate-test] submitted: ...` lines present), but no `mw3ncp_test.svg` file was ever created anywhere under `players2/save/`, and no in-game effect was observed in either Campaign or Survival. A real menu popup (`offensive_skip_popup`) that appeared in the log right after one `loadgame` test turned out to be an unrelated coincidence -- live-corrected by the user ("no thats the graphic cointent notice from the missio mind the gap") -- the London mission's own content warning, not something our command triggered.

**Conclusion: same dead-end shape as `weapnext`/`togglemenu` earlier in this project (2026-07-15, this file's own #2) -- a string existing in the binary does not mean it's a live-callable `Cmd_ExecuteString` command.** `save_name_popmenu`/`save_overwrite_popmenu` (also found in the same string scan) suggest this system is actually driven through the menu/UI action dispatcher (`resolveItemDefAction`, per the menu-command investigation elsewhere in this file), not the plain console command table -- meaning reaching it natively would need the same class of deeper RE already proven for `togglecrouch`/`weapnext` (find the real internal save-trigger function/dispatch case via disassembly, not trust a string as command syntax), not a quick console-text win. This is real, additional RE work, not yet started -- the semantic struct-mapping approach (item 4 above) remains the fallback either way, though finding the real internal save-trigger function first (if it exists as a clean, callable function) could still be a smaller win than mapping every structure from scratch.

**Consequence for the plan:** cross-relaunch save states need real semantic struct mapping (know what's a pointer, follow it, serialize to a relocatable format, rebuild it against the new launch's own heap layout on load) for anything heap-resident -- there is no shortcut via raw memory dumping. The exe's own static/global data doesn't have this problem and could still be dumped/restored directly as part of a hybrid approach. Item 4 above (real RE work to map entity/world/script-VM structures) is now confirmed as unavoidable, not just the thorough-but-optional path.

**Next step:** item 2 (check for any native save/checkpoint mechanism) is the cheapest next move and hasn't been done yet -- worth doing before starting the heavier entity/AI/GSC-VM structure-mapping RE work in item 4.

## 81. Mantle's drag handle in the in-game glyph position editor silently never worked -- RESOLVED, two real bugs, one fix each (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Resolved and confirmed live -- the fix let the user actually drag and F3-export Mantle's own calibration the same session ("i f3 for mantle now thats fixed too"), baked into `FindOrCreateGameplayHintEditNudge` (`textNudge=(-35.0f, 1.0f)`).

**Symptom:** live-reported, "the mantle drag doesnt work" -- the Mantle hint's own TEXT/ICON drag handles in the F2/F3 glyph position editor never responded to drag input, while Interact/ReadyUp/Reload's handles all worked fine.

**First fix attempt (real bug, NOT the actual blocker):** `kGameplayHintEditNudgeMax` (`overlay_hud.cpp`), the fixed-size pool `FindOrCreateGameplayHintEditNudge` allocates a persistent `(GameplayHintSlotId, FontRole)` combo slot from, was `8` -- sized for the pre-Mantle world documented in its own comment: "3 slots x 2 roles = 6 real combos, some headroom." Mantle getting its own `GameplayHintSlotId` (2026-08-25, same session, see PATCHNOTES item 9) made it 4 slots x 2 roles = 8 real combos -- exactly at capacity, zero headroom left, a genuine bug capable of returning `nullptr` for Mantle's allocation request. Bumped to 16. **Live-reported still broken afterward**: "mantle is still the only thing i cant drag since [we] make it its own group."

**What actually ruled the pool theory out:** direct clarification, "i see the bounding boxes they just aint clickable." The handle was genuinely RENDERING (which requires a non-null `editNudge`, i.e. the pool allocation had already succeeded) -- proving the first fix, while real, was never the actual blocker for this specific symptom. A `proxy_d3d9.log` capture from the same session independently confirmed the real native mantle hint (`"Press^3 Space ^7to  "`, matching the `PLATFORM_MANTLE` template) fired repeatedly and for an extended period, and traced every step of the request path (`isMantleHint` detection, `TryGetMantleGlyphAssetName`, `RequestCustomHintOverlay`'s unconditional `requestedThisFrame=true`) as structurally correct -- consistent with "renders fine."

**Real root cause:** `DrawOneGameplayHintSlot`'s own `static bool s_lastMouseHeld` (TEXT handle) and its icon-handle twin `s_lastMouseHeldIcon` were scoped to the FUNCTION, not to the slot being drawn -- but this function runs once per REQUESTED slot, every frame, and multiple hint slots can legitimately be visible in the same frame (the same `proxy_d3d9.log` capture that confirmed the mantle hint also showed ReadyUp's "Press F5 to ready up" logged in the same tight window -- ReadyUp doesn't suppress Mantle, per issue #81's own predecessor design). Since `static` locals persist across every call to the function regardless of which slot argument was passed, whichever slot got processed FIRST in a frame where two hints coexisted (fixed iteration order: Interact=0, ReadyUp=1, Reload=2, **Mantle=3, always last**) would update the one shared static to that frame's real `mouseHeld` value -- so by the time Mantle's own check ran later THAT SAME frame, `s_lastMouseHeld` already equalled `mouseHeld`, and `clickEdge = mouseHeld && !s_lastMouseHeld` could never compute `true` for Mantle whenever anything else shared its frame. Every other slot happened to get calibrated in relative isolation during this project's testing history; Mantle, always processed last in the fixed loop order, never did -- a structural reason this specific slot was uniquely affected, not coincidence.

**Fix:** both statics converted from a single function-wide bool to a small fixed array indexed by `slotId` (`kGameplayHintSlotCount` entries), so each slot tracks its own previous mouse-held state independently, the same way `g_gameplayHintEditNudges` already tracks each slot's own persistent drag offset independently.

**Lesson for future gameplay-hint editor work:** any `static` local inside `DrawOneGameplayHintSlot` (or its menu-hint counterpart, `DrawOneMenuHintSlot`, which shares the same "one function, multiple slots per frame" shape) needs to be per-slot by construction, not per-call -- a function-scoped static silently assumes "this function is called at most once per frame," which stopped being true the moment gameplay hints became a multi-slot system (BUG-004, 2026-08-02). Worth an audit of `DrawOneMenuHintSlot` for the same pattern if a similar report ever surfaces there.

**Not yet independently re-confirmed live** -- same standard this project applies to every visual/interactive fix.

## 82. Controller-glyph icons had a faint white cutout-fringe ring -- RESOLVED (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Resolved, root cause found and fixed same day; not yet visually re-confirmed live.

**Symptom:** live-reported: "for all glyphs we have to have any very faint 1-2px white ring from cutting removed entirely." Confirmed root cause via direct follow-up: "its clearly from when it was cut out they were cut well but im guessing not tight enough to avoid clippage."

**Root cause:** the source PNGs' own cutout boundaries left a thin ring of semi-transparent edge pixels that still carry the original (light/white) background color underneath, not fully cropped away. This project's icon draw path (`DrawGenericTexturedQuad`, `overlay_hud.cpp`) used standard non-premultiplied `SRCALPHA`/`INVSRCALPHA` blending, which draws a pixel's stored RGB weighted by its own alpha regardless of what that RGB actually is -- a semi-transparent edge texel storing near-white leftover RGB blends in a visible pale fringe no amount of cropping tightness alone fully avoids. D3D9's automatic mipmap generation (`D3DUSAGE_AUTOGENMIPMAP`, added 2026-08-24 for icon jaggedness, see issue #71/#74's own history) made this WORSE by box-averaging that same near-white RGB into every mip level with no regard for alpha weight, visible whenever an icon is drawn scaled down (every icon in this project's overlay is).

**Fix:** two parts, both required together:
1. `LoadGlyphIconTexture` (`overlay_hud.cpp`) now premultiplies every icon's RGB by its own alpha at load time, right after WIC decode -- a texel's stored RGB approaches 0 as its alpha approaches 0, so neither ordinary blending nor mip-level averaging has any non-zero background color left to bleed in. Applies uniformly to every asset this project loads through this one shared function (glyph icons, the custom cursor, controller diagram images) -- no per-asset special-casing needed.
2. `DrawGenericTexturedQuad` gained a new `premultipliedAlpha` parameter (default `false`, so every other existing caller -- solid white quads, the text-outline compositing system, real `.menu`-asset DDS textures via `MenuGfx_DrawTexturedQuad` -- is completely unaffected): when `true`, `SRCBLEND` switches from `SRCALPHA` to `ONE`, the correct compositing equation for already-premultiplied source data. Every one of this project's ~10 icon-cache draw call sites (direct `GetOrLoadGlyphIconTexture` consumers) was updated to pass `true`.

**Not yet independently re-confirmed live** -- same standard as issue #81 above.

## 83. Glyph-style auto-detect (Xbox 360, Xbox Modern, PlayStation) -- PREVIEW/WIP, not live-tested (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Implemented, builds clean, NOT yet live-tested against real hardware of any kind (Xbox 360, Xbox One/Series, or DualSense). Treat as PREVIEW/WIP per this project's own labeling convention until confirmed.

**The ask:** user-requested, "that thing i mentioned about making there be a default option for glyphs which detects controller type ps/xbox/xbmodern and sets accordingly" -- `GlyphStyle` (task #6, `mod_config.h`) has existed since 2026-07-21 but always required a manual, hand-edited-INI choice; XInput itself genuinely cannot distinguish an Xbox-branded pad from a third-party one, or a 360 controller from a Series controller, at the API level (this project's own long-standing documented limitation, see `GlyphStyle`'s own enum comment) -- so auto-detection needed a signal outside XInput entirely.

**What actually enables this now, that didn't exist when `GlyphStyle` was first added:** this project's own native DualSense HID backend (issue #76), which already opens a raw HID handle independent of XInput and exposes `DualSense_IsOpen()` as a cheap, already-proven "is a real DualSense currently connected" signal -- zero new HID work needed for the PlayStation case. For Xbox, a new best-effort read-only HID enumeration (`TryDetectXboxGlyphStyle`, `dualsense_input.cpp`, same `SetupDiGetClassDevsW`/`HidD_GetAttributes` pattern `TryOpenDualSense` already uses, but read-only -- `GENERIC_READ` only, never opens for exclusive read-write, so it can't contend with `controller_input.cpp`'s own XInput polling for the same physical device) scans for Microsoft's vendor ID (`0x045E`) and classifies the product ID against a small table (Xbox 360 wired/wireless PIDs -> `Xbox360`; Xbox One/Elite/S/Series PIDs -> `XboxModern`; any other `0x045E` PID -> `XboxModern` by default, since a newer/less common pad is more likely to be missing from the table than an old one).

**This table is public knowledge (used by, among others, SDL2's game controller DB and the Linux kernel's `xpad` driver), NOT independently verified against real hardware by this project across every generation.** Flagged explicitly, same honesty standard as the DualSense backend's own byte-offset table -- don't cite this PID list as confirmed-correct without a live test across at least one real controller of each classified generation.

**Design decisions:**
- New `[Bindings] GlyphStyleAuto` config key, default `true` for a fresh install. `ConfigVersion` bumped 19->20 (`mod_config.cpp`).
- **Detection runs ONCE per session**, not on a recurring timer -- deliberately, to match this project's own existing "restart to switch controller device families" design (`controller_input.cpp`'s `XInputPollThreadProc`, locks onto XInput or DualSense for the life of the process). Continuously re-polling for glyph style independently of that lock would be inconsistent with it, and could misreport PlayStation glyphs while the actual locked input source is still an XInput translator layer (e.g. Steam Input presenting a DualSense as a virtual XInput pad) -- exactly the class of confusion the native DualSense backend was built to route around in the first place (issue #74/#76). The detection call sits directly at both of `XInputPollThreadProc`'s own `g_lockedSource = ...` assignment points.
- **Migration for existing configs:** since `GlyphStyleAuto` is a brand-new key, a plain "absent key defaults to compiled default" migration would risk silently overriding a player who'd hand-edited `GlyphStyle` to `XboxModern`/`PlayStation` before this feature existed (the only way to set it away from `Xbox360` before now, since no in-game selector control exists). `LoadModConfig` (`mod_config.cpp`) checks the ALREADY-loaded `GlyphStyle` value as a stand-in signal: if the `GlyphStyleAuto` key is absent AND `GlyphStyle` isn't sitting at its historical `Xbox360` default, `GlyphStyleAuto` defaults to `false` instead of `true` -- same "explicit value always wins" policy this project already applies to `FontItalic`'s own default flip (2026-08-24).

**Not yet done:** no in-game UI control to toggle `GlyphStyleAuto` or manually override it exists yet (INI-only, same as `GlyphStyle` itself always has been) -- would need the eventual custom Options screen work (deprioritized until v0.3.6, post-LTS, per the project's own LTS plan). No live test performed this session against any real controller of any generation -- purely a build-clean, logically-reviewed implementation.

**Status:** Open, reported, not yet investigated. Logged so the observation isn't lost, not acted on this pass -- not enough detail yet to know which real group/depth this actually is.

Reading a pause-menu screen's right-side panel (context not yet pinned down further -- could be a stat/preview panel, a description panel, or a genuinely separate list; not established which) with the in-game glyph position editor active, the editor's own selection-tracking DOES pick up a real focused item there (implying `TryGetRealFocusedGroupAndIndex` or the equivalent ordinal-fallback signal is genuinely firing on this panel), but no glyph is ever drawn.

**Why "no glyph draws" is expected, not itself the bug:** this matches issue #51's own standing design exactly -- a real selection signal firing with no on-screen glyph is exactly what an UNVERIFIED group looks like under the current allowlist model (`kVerifiedGlyphGroups`/`kManualGlyphPositions`): detection existing doesn't mean a table entry exists for that specific `(groupName, depth)`, and this project deliberately draws nothing rather than a possibly-wrong position for anything not on the allowlist. So this observation isn't "detection is broken" -- it's "here's a screen with a real, working selection signal that's never had a calibration pass," the same category as every other row in issue #51's own coverage table.

Worth a dedicated F3/diagnostic-logging pass (`HudGlyphPositionLogging`/`ListItemPositionLogging`, both already wired into this project's existing tooling) the next time this screen is reached, to capture the real group name and confirm whether it's a new entry for `kManualGlyphPositions` or an existing one just never exercised from this specific navigation path.

**Next step:** reproduce with logging enabled, capture the real group/depth from `proxy_d3d9.log`, then decide whether it's covered by an existing table entry (just needs `kVerifiedGlyphGroups` added) or is a genuinely new screen needing its own calibration pass.

## 85. Plugin API (hook installation, memory read/write, text/glyph color override) -- CONFIRMED WORKING LIVE (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Confirmed working live the same session -- direct user report: "plugin layer works like a charm too." The loader found/loaded/initialized the RGB Text example plugin against the real running game and the `SetTextGlyphColorOverride` extension point visibly rainbow-cycles real in-game text/glyphs as designed. Still PREVIEW/WIP in the sense that only this one example plugin has ever been built against the API -- the ABI itself is young and could still need adjustment once a second, different plugin is written against it.

**Strategic observation (2026-08-25, same session, direct user framing): "this plugin api is essentialy for mw3 itself not only our mod. this is huge in terms of our mod for adoption as plugins are essentially sub mods."** Correct and worth recording explicitly -- `InstallHook`/`ReadMemory`/`WriteMemory` operate on the real game process, not a sandboxed view of this mod's own state, so a plugin isn't limited to reskinning/extending MW32011NCP's own UI (the way the RGB Text example does) -- it can hook or touch any part of `iw5sp.exe`/`iw5mp.exe` a plugin author chooses to target. In effect, MW32011NCP now doubles as a lightweight loader/platform for MW3 sub-mods generally, with this mod's own controller layer as the first real consumer of that surface, not the limit of it. This reframes the API's significance beyond "an extension point for our own mod" -- genuinely relevant to this project's own adoption/positioning, not just a technical detail. `PLUGIN_API.md` and `README.md` both updated to state this explicitly.

**The ask:** user-requested, "i also think now is the time to start developing our own api for plugins which will get immense control over stuff and be able to add non vac safe things. not something we ship as part of the main mod." Clarified via direct scoping questions: **the plugin API and its loading surface ship as part of the main mod's own compiled `d3d9.dll`** -- only actual built plugin DLLs are excluded from the main mod's release packaging. API surface, per direct answer: hook-installation primitives (reusing this project's existing MinHook infrastructure) + direct process memory read/write. Later clarified further: plugins aren't only for that class of thing -- "plugins dont have to be for stuff like that and can be used for any extension of the mod," with an explicit request to ship a real, working example: "RGB text which uses our already made rainbow shader on all mod wide text and glyphs."

**Why this doesn't reopen the aim-assist decision:** the main mod's own permanently-removed aim-assist feature established a hard-line policy against the MAIN MOD reading live gameplay-entity memory (`known_issues.md` issue #33). The plugin API is a deliberately separate, explicitly opt-in (`[Plugins] Enabled=0` by default), not-shipped-plugin extension point -- the loader infrastructure ships inert, and the capability only does anything once the user explicitly enables it AND drops a plugin DLL in themselves. See `PLUGIN_API.md`'s own risk statement, written specifically so this distinction is never lost on a future session.

**Design, implemented:**
- New `[Plugins] Enabled` config key (`mod_config.h`/`.cpp`, `ConfigVersion` 20->21), default off, same "strictly opt-in" pattern as `AutoMantleEnabled`/`UseCustomOptionsScreen`.
- `proxy_d3d9/src/mw3ncp_plugin_api.h` -- the public, plain-C, stable-ABI plugin header (`MW3NCP_PluginAPI` struct, `MW3NCP_PLUGIN_API_VERSION`). No C++ types cross the boundary, matching this project's own established `MenuGfx_*`/`tools/ui_harness` cross-boundary convention.
- `proxy_d3d9/src/plugin_loader.h`/`.cpp` -- scans `<dll_dir>\plugins\*.dll`, loads anything exporting `MW3NCP_PluginInit`, logs every step (found/loaded/rejected/initialized) unconditionally. `InstallHook`/`RemoveHook` are thin wrappers around the host's own already-initialized MinHook instance (no second `MH_Initialize`, so a plugin and the host can't silently stomp each other's hooks via independent instances). `ReadMemory`/`WriteMemory` are SEH-guarded (`__try`/`__except (EXCEPTION_EXECUTE_HANDLER)`), returning 0 instead of crashing on an inaccessible page.
- New extension point beyond raw hook/memory access: `SetTextGlyphColorOverride(callback)` -- a plugin-registerable `unsigned long(unsigned long)` callback consulted by `DrawGenericTexturedQuad` (`overlay_hud.cpp`) whenever a new `isTextOrGlyph` parameter is true. That parameter was threaded through every text and controller-glyph-icon draw call site in the file (gameplay hints via the shared `drawScaledQuad` lambda, menu hints via its own twin, the highlighted-item A-glyph, diagram-editor labels/icons, list A-glyph icons, the corner Back icon+text, the custom Options screen's own text via `DrawOptLeftAlignedText`/`DrawOptRightAlignedText`, and the `tools/ui_harness`-facing `MenuGfx_DrawLeftText` forwarder) -- while solid UI chrome (progress bars, sliders, panel backgrounds), the custom cursor, and the controller-body diagram photo were deliberately left `false`, since this is specifically a "text and glyphs" cosmetic surface, not a general rendering hook.
- `tools/example_plugin_rgb_text/` -- a real, working plugin (not a stub): reuses the exact hue-cycle math this mod's own toast-notification `OverlayAnimStyle::Rainbow` already uses (duplicated, not shared -- a plugin is a separately-built DLL and can't reach the host's own internal functions), registers it via `SetTextGlyphColorOverride`. This is both a real usable dev-test/novelty plugin and the live-verification vehicle for the plugin API itself, per this project's own Production Readiness Criteria (code that only compiles isn't done).

**Not yet done:** the API surface is intentionally minimal/developer-facing for this first pass -- direct user framing, "in future the api should be made more user friendly but for now this is what is needed for devs." A friendlier, higher-level API is a real intended direction, deliberately deferred until real plugins exist to learn from, not designed speculatively ahead of need.

**Live confirmation (2026-08-25, same session):** deployed to the live install (`[Plugins] Enabled=1`, `rgb_text_plugin.dll` in `plugins\`), relaunched, and confirmed working -- "plugin layer works like a charm too." Both halves proven: the loader (found, loaded, and initialized the example plugin) and the `SetTextGlyphColorOverride` extension point (the rainbow effect actually renders on real text/glyphs in-game, not just in isolation).

## 86. "B Back" corner hint shows twice on Survival buy-station screens, 3 layers deep -- RESOLVED, confirmed live for buy stations (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Resolved, real root cause identified directly by the user (not this session's own first guess, see below); fixed and confirmed live the same session. Direct user report: "popup menus seem fixed though i tested buy stations only." **Confirmed specifically for the reported case (Survival buy stations, 3 layers deep) -- other popup-modal families (main menu "Choose Game Mode," Special Ops nested modals, etc.) that could theoretically hit the same position-tolerance gap have NOT been separately re-tested**, since the `isBackShortcut` role-based dedup is a general fix (not scoped to buy stations specifically), it should cover them too, but that's an inference from the fix's own design, not an independent live confirmation for those other screens.

**Symptom:** live-reported, "another issue that resurfaced is that 'B back' shows twice on the buy station screens when you go 3 layers deep into it i think."

**First hypothesis (WRONG, superseded, kept here for the record per this project's own "document a wrong-but-real first fix honestly" standard):** this session initially suspected a stale `g_specOpsModalSticky` flag firing `InjectSyntheticBackHintIfNeeded`'s synthetic Back hint on top of the buy station's own real one. A diagnostic log line was added to check this. **Directly corrected by the user before that diagnostic ever got a chance to run**: "the b back thing is because the 3rd deep screen is bigger, so the other screen is under but our mod still draws the B, we can fix this easy just suppress the old draw from screen 2 when on screen 3 ... for popup modals in specific." The diagnostic and its associated dead state variable were removed once the real cause was known -- see git history for the brief-lived version, not worth keeping the diagnostic around, this fix path was empirically wrong.

**Real root cause:** when a popup modal (screen 3) visually covers a smaller screen underneath it (screen 2), the underlying screen's own real native corner-hint draw call STILL fires every frame -- the game doesn't know or care it's obscured, same general class of issue `RequestMenuHintOverlay`'s own existing position-tolerance dedup was originally built to solve (2026-08-01, the Friends-vs-Special-Ops-modal case). That existing fix collapses two Back-ish hints into one slot ONLY when they land within `kSamePositionToleragePx` (20px) of each other -- true for the standard main-menu corner convention it was built against, but **not** guaranteed true for every popup family: a Survival buy-station popup's own real corner-hint position can differ enough from the screen it covers that the position-tolerance check simply doesn't catch it, leaving both as genuinely separate slots -- both drawn, both visible, reading as "shows twice."

**Fix:** added a second, ROLE-based dedup alongside the existing position-based one. `MenuHintSlot` gained a new `bool isBackShortcut` field; `RequestMenuHintOverlay` gained a matching `isBackShortcut` parameter (default `false`) -- when `true`, the request first checks for ANY other slot already marked `isBackShortcut` this frame (regardless of position) and overwrites that one instead of relying on pixel proximity. Same "last call wins approximates native paint order" reasoning the position-based fix already uses (Hook_DrawGlyphText calls happen in real draw order, so the popup's own Back hint is naturally requested after the screen it covers), just keyed on semantic identity for this one specific, always-unique hint instead of screen position. Wired at both real call sites: the generic `PLATFORM_BACK_SHORTCUT` detection (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`, hoisted into a named `isBackShortcut` bool the same way `isFriendsShortcut` already was) and `RequestSyntheticBackHint` (the Special Ops synthetic path, issue #81's own investigation target -- now also correctly collapses with a real Back hint the same frame instead of potentially coexisting as a second slot).

**Confirmed live (2026-08-25, same session)** for the reported case -- Survival buy stations, 3 layers deep. See the Status line above for the scope of what's confirmed vs. inferred.

## 87. Recurring freeze every 2-5 seconds -- THREE real, evidence-backed causes found and fixed; not yet live-confirmed (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Three real causes found and fixed this investigation (poll-thread cadence, main-thread vibration writes, main-thread config-hot-reload file-stat call). **Not yet live-confirmed** -- needs a real play session to confirm the freezes are actually gone.

**Investigation history (each cause found via real evidence or a real external test, not guessed):**
1. Controller poll thread free-ran on a fixed 250Hz clock regardless of real demand (below).
2. `Controller_SetVibration` called `XInputSetState`/`DualSense_SetVibration` synchronously on the game's own gameplay-tick thread (below, "Vibration writes" section).
3. `CheckConfigHotReload` ran an unconditional `GetFileAttributesExA` syscall on the main thread once a second, forever, with zero instrumentation anywhere (below, "Config hot-reload" section) -- the strongest, most specific candidate, found by a fork diffing v0.2.2 against v0.2.5 after the user recalled this exact issue was NOT present on the v0.2.2 LTS build and pointed at "post-0.2.5" as when it appeared.

**Ruled out along the way:**
- **Multi-device/multi-slot polling** -- checked first, does NOT match the code; source locking already existed since v0.3.3.
- **Steam Input's own background XInput-translation layer** -- a real, well-documented community-reported stutter source matching this exact shape ("constant micro stutters every 2 seconds or so") and would have explained the XInput-vs-DualSense asymmetry, but the user confirmed Steam Input was already disabled for this game. Ruled out directly, not guessed.
- **This project's own overlay/glyph draw code** -- user's own direct theory ("something with us drawing over the game caused issues with framerate stability"). A real `frametime_benchmark.csv` capture (30676 frames) showed `ourOwnTotalMs` (sum of every instrumented hook: options menu, overlay message, glyph icon, hint slots, rumble, asset capture, texture creation) at p50=0.0003ms, p99=0.24ms, max=1.48ms across the whole session -- negligible and flat, including during the session's own largest frametime spikes. Directly contradicts this theory for the captured session.
- **The engine's native 30Hz-simulation/60Hz-present frame pattern** (odd-indexed frames averaging ~15.2ms, even-indexed ~1.4ms, alternating throughout the whole log) -- confirmed this is a rock-solid, non-anomalous pattern (odd-frame p999=16.4ms), not a bug or a "spike," just this old engine's own known frame-pacing.
- **A one-off 76-136ms burst at the very tail of the captured session** (frames 30535-30552 of 30676) -- real, but clustered in a narrow 17-frame window right at session end, not a recurring every-2-5s pattern; very likely a shutdown/quit artifact, not the reported issue.

**Symptom, live-reported (in order):** "so the lag spikes are still happening and way more on xniput than on ps controller, gotta be that polling bs we should cut the polling and just use the first controller that input is detected from and stop polling" -- then, after the poll-thread fix alone: "its not eben that so i can rule out the polling, vibration etc, something is causing a major instability in the engine itself as afterburner doesnt detect it" -- then, after ruling out Steam Input and re-examining the frametime capture: "my conclusion is definitive, something with us drawing over the game caused issues with the framerate stability look at the logs" (see "Ruled out along the way" above for why the data didn't support this) -- then, decisively: "remember we tested this exact issue before and it wasnt present on the current LTS," redirecting the investigation to a v0.2.2-vs-post-0.2.5 diff, which is what actually found cause #3.

### Cause 1: Controller poll thread free-ran on a fixed 250Hz clock regardless of real demand

**Symptom, live-reported:** "so the lag spikes are still happening and way more on xniput than on ps controller, gotta be that polling bs we should cut the polling and just use the first controller that input is detected from and stop polling."

**Checked before changing anything, per this project's own "checking is far cheaper than digging" standard:** the user's stated theory (multiple controllers/slots being scanned) does NOT match the actual code -- source LOCKING already existed since v0.3.3 (`LockedInputSource`, `g_lockedSource`, never reset once set): once one device locks in, the poll thread never re-scans other XInput slots or attempts DualSense again, full stop, for the rest of the process. Confirmed by direct code review of `controller_input.cpp` before proposing any fix.

**Real issue: the poll thread's steady-state CADENCE, not its scope.** Even fully locked onto one source, the background thread ran an unconditional `for(;;) { poll; Sleep(kPollIntervalMs); }` loop at a fixed 250Hz (`kPollIntervalMs = 4`) -- calling `XInputGetState`/`DualSense_Poll` on its own independent clock 250 times a second regardless of whether the game actually needed fresh input that specific tick. Real, avoidable overhead, and per the live report, `XInputGetState`'s own per-call cost appears to be noticeably higher than DualSense's raw-HID blocking `ReadFile` -- plausible if the XInput path is going through a virtual/translator layer (Steam Input) rather than a direct driver, and consistent with "worse on XInput than PS controller."

**User-suggested external reference, checked before implementing:** "lets use x360ce as reference no?" -- fetched x360ce's real source (`Controller.cpp`, via `gh api search/code` + raw GitHub fetch, not guessed) and found it has **no background poll thread at all**: its own `GetState()` just forwards straight to the real `XInputGetState()` synchronously, called on-demand whenever the game itself asks. This directly validates that XInputGetState is designed to be called synchronously/on-demand (Windows' own driver layer already caches the real hardware poll underneath it) rather than needing an external dedicated polling thread running on its own clock -- confirms the fix direction rather than another guess.

**Fix:** replaced the fixed `Sleep(kPollIntervalMs)` with an auto-reset event wait (`WaitForSingleObject(g_pollWakeEvent, kPollWakeTimeoutMs)`, 50ms safety-net timeout only, not a real interval). Added `Controller_RequestPoll()` (`controller_input.cpp`/`.h`) -- `SetEvent`s the wake event, safe to call redundantly, lazily starts the thread/event via the same pattern every `Controller_Get*` accessor already used. Wired into the two REAL per-tick consumers, right before each reads cached state: `InjectAllControllerInput` (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`, the gameplay-tick hook) and `InjectMenuInputTick` (the WndProc/SetTimer path that keeps running during pause/menus, when the gameplay hook has already stopped firing). A poll now only ever happens when something is actually about to consume its result -- no independent clock, no reads when nothing asked for one. Keeps the background thread itself (still off the main/render thread, still handles the blocking DualSense HID read safely) -- only the CADENCE that drives it changed, from a fixed clock to real demand.

**Deliberately NOT changed:** the one-time device-detection phase (`LockedInputSource::Undetermined`) and its own internal logic are untouched -- it still runs inline inside the same poll-thread function, just now driven by the same wake-ups as everything else (both real consumers fire from very early in the process lifetime -- the WndProc's `SetTimer` guarantees ~60Hz `WM_TIMER` messages from boot -- so detection still completes quickly in practice).

**Next step:** live playtest, specifically watching for whether the XInput-side lag spikes the original report described are actually gone, not just theoretically addressed.

### Cause 2: Vibration writes called XInputSetState/DualSense_SetVibration synchronously on the game's own gameplay-tick thread

**Found by direct code review** (live-reported: "check on vibratw") -- `Controller_SetVibration` called `g_XInputSetState`/`DualSense_SetVibration` directly on whichever thread called it, which for every real call site in this codebase is `Rumble_Tick()`, called from `InjectAllControllerInput` -- the game's own gameplay-tick thread. This directly contradicted this file's own original 2026-08-08 design goal for the background poll thread ("moving ALL real XInputGetState/XInputSetState calls onto a single dedicated background thread... no matter how slow any individual XInput call is, it can never again block the main thread") -- SetState had been carved out of that move on an unverified "cheap/idempotent" assumption, never actually confirmed via the `FrameBenchmark_AddRumbleMs` instrumentation sitting right next to the call (added 2026-08-17, exactly for this suspicion, never conclusively resolved either way).

**Fix:** `Controller_SetVibration` no longer touches hardware at all -- it clamps the requested motor values, stashes them in a new `g_pendingVibration` struct (guarded by the existing `g_stateLock`), and calls `Controller_RequestPoll()` to wake the poll thread. A new `ApplyPendingVibrationOnPollThread()` (called once per poll-thread wake cycle, right alongside the input read) performs the actual `XInputSetState`/`DualSense_SetVibration` write -- on the background thread, never the game's own thread, matching cause 1's fix pattern exactly. `FrameBenchmark_AddRumbleMs` still times the real write, just on its new thread -- a real number there no longer implies a stutter risk the way it would have before this moved.

### Cause 3: CheckConfigHotReload ran an uninstrumented, unconditional GetFileAttributesExA on the main thread every second, forever -- strongest candidate, dated exactly right

**Found by a fork diffing `v0.2.2` against `v0.2.5`**, directed by the user's own recollection that this exact issue was absent on the v0.2.2 LTS build. `CheckConfigHotReload` (`mod_config.cpp`), added in v0.2.5's config-hot-reload QoL feature (2026-07-31), ran the ENTIRE file-change check -- including the actual `GetFileAttributesExA` syscall -- directly on the main thread, rate-limited to once per second but otherwise unconditional, for the entire process lifetime, called from `InjectMenuInputTick` (the always-running WndProc/SetTimer tick). `GetFileAttributesExA` is normally a cheap cached NTFS stat, but is a well-documented real-world stutter source when antivirus real-time protection intercepts the file-system call -- an IRREGULAR stall (only some calls get intercepted, not all), which matches the reported "random," not perfectly periodic character better than a deterministic engine-side cause would.

**Why this evaded two separate diagnostic passes (this one and issue #79's own earlier investigation):** `frametime_benchmark.csv`/`frame_benchmark.h` has no instrumentation column for this call at all -- it only ever timed rumble, asset-capture, and real `CreateTexture` costs. A stall here shows as pure `frameTimeMs` cost with every one of this project's own measured columns reading near-zero -- exactly the pattern this session's own capture showed. Afterburner also wouldn't reliably catch a sub-frame main-thread stall unless it happened to land inside a `Present`-to-`Present` window it was actively sampling.

**Fix:** split into two halves, same pattern as causes 1 and 2. A new dedicated background thread (`ConfigHotReloadThreadProc`, `mod_config.cpp`) does the actual `GetFileAttributesExA` call and `CompareFileTime` check once a second, forever, off the main thread -- setting a `g_configFileChangedPending` flag (guarded by a new `g_hotReloadLock`) if the file genuinely changed. `CheckConfigHotReload` (still called every tick from `InjectMenuInputTick`, unchanged call sites) now just checks and consumes that flag -- the actual reload (`LoadModConfig`/`InvalidateTextTextureCachesOnConfigChange`/`ShowOverlayMessage`) stays on the main thread exactly as before, since those touch plain, unsynchronized globals that are only ever safe to read/write from the main thread (the same constraint `controller_input.cpp`'s own toast-handoff comment already documents for `ShowOverlayMessage`) -- only the potentially-slow stat call itself moved.

**Not yet independently confirmed as THE cause** -- strong circumstantial match (right release, right thread, right call pattern, a real documented Windows stutter mechanism, invisible to every tool already tried), but not proven by a direct repro/capture correlating an AV interception event to a felt stutter.

**Live-retested after causes 1-3 deployed**: "its a bit better but there is still hitching" -- real improvement, not resolved. Also newly confirmed: **the PS5/DualSense controller stutters too**, not just XInput -- this actually strengthens (not weakens) the causes-2/3 theory over any XInput-specific one (Steam Input, already ruled out): a main-thread-wide stall from vibration writes or config-hot-reload would affect both controller backends equally, which is exactly what's now being reported, whereas a genuinely XInput-only mechanism would not explain a DualSense stutter at all.

### Cause 4: Log()'s periodic fflush() also ran on whichever calling thread crossed the 1-second interval

**Found via direct user framing: "i/o is a huge candidate."** `Log()` (`dllmain.cpp`) already had a real, deliberate fix from an earlier session (2026-08-08) for a different problem -- flushing on EVERY call was too expensive, so it was throttled to flush at most once every `kLogFlushIntervalMs` (1000ms) instead. But the throttle only gated WHEN the flush happens, not WHICH THREAD does it: the actual `fflush()` still ran synchronously on whatever thread's `Log()` call happened to cross that 1-second threshold -- and since the vast majority of this project's ~180 log call sites fire from the game's own main thread, that's almost always where the flush landed. Exactly the same bug class as cause 3 (`GetFileAttributesExA`): a disk write that's normally cheap but a well-documented stutter source when antivirus real-time protection intercepts it, invisible to `frametime_benchmark.csv` (no instrumentation column for logging at all) and to Afterburner (a sub-frame main-thread stall doesn't reliably show as a Present-to-Present gap).

**Fix:** same split pattern as causes 1-3. `Log()` now only ever calls `fprintf()` (buffered, cheap, no disk I/O per call -- MSVC's CRT already internally locks a `FILE*` per operation, so concurrent `fprintf`/`fflush` calls from different threads on the same stream are safe without an explicit lock here). A new dedicated `LogFlushThreadProc` background thread (started once from `LogInit`, alongside the existing crash-flush vectored exception handler which stays unchanged) sleeps `kLogFlushIntervalMs` and calls `fflush(g_log)` in a loop, completely decoupled from every real log call site. The one-time attach-line flush in `LogInit` itself stays inline (runs once, at DLL attach, not a hot path).

Builds clean (0 warnings/errors). Deployed pending the game being closed. Not yet live-confirmed.

### Self-audit: could this session's OWN new threading be the cause, not fixing it?

**Prompted by direct user question: "what if. like you said when i requested it, threading is whats causing the issue."** A fair, important check, not dismissed -- this session added two new always-on background threads (config-hot-reload, log-flush) on top of the pre-existing controller-poll thread, all within a short window, which is exactly the kind of change that could itself introduce a regression.

**Found one real, self-inflicted regression risk, fixed:** `Controller_RequestPoll()` (cause 1's own fix) is called unconditionally at the top of `InjectMenuInputTick` -- which, per this project's own 2026-08-08 history, fires on EVERY WndProc message, not just its own ~60Hz `WM_TIMER`, including "dozens of times per rendered frame" during mouse movement (the EXACT flood pattern that caused the original 4fps regression the whole background-poll-thread architecture was built to prevent in the first place). `SetEvent()` is far cheaper than the `XInputGetState` call that caused that original bug, but it's a real kernel transition, and calling it unconditionally from that same flood-prone path risked reintroducing a smaller version of the identical bug class. **Fixed:** `Controller_RequestPoll()` is now throttled to once per `kMinPollRequestIntervalMs` (15ms) regardless of how many times a caller invokes it in one frame -- keeps the "poll on real demand" design while capping the worst case.

**The other two new threads (config-hot-reload, log-flush) assessed as low-risk:** both are simple `Sleep(1000)`-loop background threads doing a single cheap syscall once a second, with no per-frame interaction with the main thread beyond a lightweight flag/critical-section check inside `CheckConfigHotReload`/nothing at all for logging. Not ruled out with certainty (no live profiling data on these specifically), but structurally a very different risk profile from the SetEvent-flood bug actually found and fixed above.

Builds clean (0 warnings/errors). Deployed.

**Live-retested after the SetEvent rate-limit fix**: "still has stutters but is less frequent, theres gotta be more" -- real, further improvement, still not resolved.

### Cause 5: MeasureTextWidthPx had no cache at all -- a real GDI cost paid every frame

**Found by a systematic fork audit** of every remaining Windows API call in the codebase that could plausibly run on the main thread during normal gameplay, dispatched specifically to widen the search past the "disk I/O" shape of causes 1-4 (this one is GDI/font work, not file I/O -- no AV-interception angle, a genuinely different bug class). `MeasureTextWidthPx` (`overlay_hud.cpp`) does a full `GetDC`/`CreateFontA`/`GetTextExtentPoint32A`/`SelectObject`(restore)/`DeleteObject`/`ReleaseDC` round-trip on every single call, with **no cache whatsoever** -- confirmed by direct comparison against its own sibling function, `EnsureLeftAlignedTextTexture` (the function that actually renders the text into a texture), which DOES have a real cache keyed on text+font-height and only re-renders on genuine change. `MeasureTextWidthPx` sits right next to every one of those cached-render calls in `DrawOneGameplayHintSlot`/`DrawOneMenuHintSlot` (prefix/suffix/top-line width) but never got the equivalent guard -- paying a fresh GDI round-trip every frame for as long as any gameplay hint or menu corner hint is visible, which is most of normal play (interact prompts, reload reminder, ready-up, buy stations, mantle, every menu screen's corner hints). Also hit every frame the custom Options screen is open (off by default).

**Fix:** added `g_measuredTextWidthCache`, a small (48-entry) fixed array cache keyed on (text, italic, fontHeightPx, fontRole) -- linear-scan (call volume per frame is a handful, not thousands, so no need for a hash table), round-robin eviction when full. `MeasureTextWidthPx` now checks this cache before doing any real GDI work. Wired into the existing `InvalidateTextTextureCachesOnConfigChange` (`ClearMeasureTextWidthCache()`), alongside every other text cache, so a live `FontFamily`/`FontFamilyCondensed`/`FontItalic` config change still takes effect correctly rather than leaving stale widths measured against the old font.

Each individual GDI call here is normally sub-millisecond, so this is a real but smaller-magnitude fix than causes 1-4 -- a genuine, uncapped per-frame cost with an obvious, already-proven-correct fix pattern sitting right next to it, not a guess.

Builds clean (0 warnings/errors). Deployed.

### Likely explanation for whatever residual remains: native GPU-bound cost at resolutions above 1080p, not this mod's own code

**Live-retested after all five fixes; also live-tested a genuinely new angle: "at 1080p i notice none of that but at 1440p it was a mess.. is it our scaling!!!"** -- followed up directly: **"yeah ive tested 4:3 its fine on that too, just res above 1080P my guess is the engine supports it poorly."** A clean, decisive correlation: 4:3 fine, 1080p fine, anything above 1080p breaks.

Checked this project's own resolution-scaling code before accepting the theory (per this project's own "checking is far cheaper than digging" standard, same as every other candidate this session) -- see issue #79's own "Real correlation found" addendum for the full detail. No bug found: 1440p is exactly 16:9 like 1080p (`GetResolutionScale` computes `scaleX == scaleY` at both, unlike the real, already-fixed non-16:9 distortion bug this project had before), independently confirmed correct at 1440p by a real user report in an earlier session, and no per-pixel loop or resolution-scaled render target exists anywhere in the normal gameplay draw path.

**Conclusion:** whatever hitching remains after this session's five real fixes is very likely a genuine native GPU-bound rendering-cost ceiling this old engine hits above its original console-era 1080p target -- issue #79's own still-parked "GPU-bound" theory, now with a real, specific resolution correlation behind it, not something further changes to this mod's own code can fix. **Not proven by real GPU profiling** (RenderDoc/PIX, still never done) -- a strong correlation, not a confirmed root cause. If pursued further, that's the next real step, not another code audit of this project's own hooks.

### Cause 6 (thread-safety hardening, not a new bug): vibration writes given their own dedicated thread, separate from input polling

**Direct follow-up request**: "i also think that im seeing cpu spikes which could be responsibe for the hitches now as i retesed 1440 and its definitely better but i wouldnt say 100% fixed, we need thread safety and a fallback threa[d]" -- clarified: "if a thread is overloaded etc can take the load off." A genuine thread-safety self-audit was done first (see the "Self-audit" section above, extended here): every lock added this session (`g_stateLock` for `g_pendingVibration`, `g_hotReloadLock` for the config-hot-reload flag, the CRT's own internal per-`FILE*` locking for the log) was confirmed correctly used, no new race found. The CPU-spike observation itself is most likely the SAME resolution-correlated native GPU cost above, not a new independent cause -- when the GPU can't keep up, the CPU often spikes doing sync/wait work (stalling on the command queue, waiting inside `Present`), which reads as CPU load even though the root cause is GPU-side.

**Real, separate improvement made anyway**: vibration writes (`ApplyPendingVibration`) originally shared the SAME background thread as input polling -- correct (off the main thread) but meant a slow/stalled input read could delay a queued vibration write behind it in the same sequential loop, and vice versa. Given a new dedicated thread (`VibrationThreadProc`, its own auto-reset wake event `g_vibrationWakeEvent`, started via `EnsureVibrationThreadStarted`) so a stall in either input polling or vibration writes can never block the other -- genuine load separation between two logically distinct jobs that happened to share one thread, not just "off the main thread" (already true before this). Renamed `ApplyPendingVibrationOnPollThread` -> `ApplyPendingVibration` to match (it no longer runs on the poll thread). Deliberately did NOT build a literal redundant "fallback poller" that duplicates the primary input-polling thread's own work -- this project has already hit the exact "two things reading the same source fight each other" bug class once before (DualSense-vs-XInput poll-priority contention, and the Steam Input theory checked earlier this session), so a duplicate poller would risk reintroducing that, not fixing anything.

Builds clean (0 warnings/errors). Deployed. Not yet live-confirmed.
