## 88. Internal render resolution — RESOLVED: 1920x1080 is a per-profile `r_mode` config value, NOT a hardcoded engine cap — tracks the real in-game Video resolution setting (2026-08-25)

**Status:** Resolved. The open question left by this issue's earlier pass ("does the 1920x1080 viewport track the in-game Video resolution setting, or is it a hardcoded cap independent of it?") is answered by real disassembly evidence this project already had sitting in `re_notes/iw5sp.md` (its own "Render-resolution 'cap': REFUTED as a hard engine limit" section, ~line 3260, same 2026-08-25 session) but had not yet cross-referenced against this issue. No live test was needed — static RE already settles it with higher confidence than a single live capture would.

**The resolving finding, from `re_notes/iw5sp.md`:** `FindStringRefs` on `"r_mode"` led to `FUN_006798e0`, decompiled in full — the real resolution-list-building function. It calls the genuine `IDirect3D9::GetAdapterModeCount`/`EnumAdapterModes` vtable methods (`vtable+0x18`/`vtable+0x1c`) to build the Resolution dropdown's option list live from the actual display adapter's supported modes — every mode ≥640x480 is kept, deduplicated, sorted, and stringified into the `r_mode` enum dvar's value list. This monitor's real native 2560x1440 is genuinely one of the enumerable, selectable entries, not excluded by any list-building logic. The DEFAULT/current index is chosen by a saved per-profile config value (`DAT_021cd930`/`DAT_021cd934`/`DAT_021cd938`, gating a search for a stored width/height match), falling back to index 0 of the sorted list only if no saved preference exists.

**Conclusion:** the 1920x1080 viewport this issue originally measured (backbuffer=2560x1440, GetViewport=1920x1080) is this specific install/profile's SAVED `r_mode` value — most likely MW3's own 2011-era factory default, or a value never updated to match a newer >1080p monitor — not an engine-enforced ceiling. The real enumeration/selection code would happily render at native 2560x1440 if the in-game Video resolution dropdown were set to it. **This means Feature 2 (internal render resolution control) does not need new engine-hooking work to unlock either direction** — the engine already exposes a real, live, user-selectable resolution control via its own native `r_mode` dvar and Options-menu Resolution dropdown; a player (or this project, via `real_settings.h`'s existing `GetDvarString`/`SetDvar`-style helpers) can already set internal render resolution to anything the display enumerates, both above and below the window/display size, with zero custom rendering-pipeline code.

**Original measurements (still accurate, reinterpreted above), for reference, from THIS session's own `proxy_d3d9.log`:**
- `[d3d9-hook] [res-diag] backbuffer=2560x1440 windowClient=2560x1440` (`d3d9_hook.cpp`'s `Hook_CreateDevice` diagnostic, added 2026-08-16) -- the real D3D9 backbuffer requested at device-creation time MATCHES the real window size, 2560x1440. No mismatch here.
- `[overlay-hud][res-scale] real screen size=1920x1080 vp.X=0 vp.Y=0 (source=GetViewport)` (`GetResolutionScale`'s own diagnostic, `overlay_hud.cpp`, added for the SEPARATE issue #51 glyph-editor investigation on 2026-08-16 and never revisited for this question) -- the real, live `IDirect3DDevice9::GetViewport` call during actual rendering returns 1920x1080, not 2560x1440, with a zero origin (not a pillarboxed/letterboxed sub-region, a genuinely smaller full viewport).

**Conclusion: the engine creates a full-size 2560x1440 backbuffer but only ever actually RENDERS into a 1920x1080 region of it** (the remaining backbuffer area is presumably either stretched into or left unused -- which of the two wasn't determined this pass, see Next Step below). This directly confirms, with real numbers for the first time, the internal-vs-window render-resolution mismatch this project's own `GetResolutionScale` comment already flagged from an EARLIER, separate live report (2026-08-16, issue #51: "2560x1440 window / 1920x1080 viewport") -- that finding was real and reproduced again today, just never connected to the CreateDevice-time backbuffer diagnostic living in a different file until this pass.

**Real reframing of issue #87's own "GPU-bound cost scales with resolution above 1080p" theory -- narrows it, doesn't invalidate it.** If this engine's actual 3D rendering workload is genuinely fixed at 1920x1080 regardless of window/display size, then the "1440p is a mess, 1080p is fine" symptom is NOT simply "more pixels to render at 1440p" the way a naive resolution-scaling-cost theory would assume -- the real render workload may be identical either way. The extra cost at higher window/display sizes more likely comes from something else layered on top of that fixed-resolution render: the stretch-blit/upscale step itself (a real, if usually cheap, GPU operation, but one this old engine may implement inefficiently), Windows' own desktop composition (DWM) scaling a smaller backbuffer region to fill a larger window, or a genuinely separate cost unrelated to the render resolution question at all. **Does not undo the real resolution correlation the user found (1080p/4:3 fine, above 1080p a mess)** -- that correlation is still real and still the strongest lead this project has for issue #87's residual -- but the underlying MECHANISM may be different from "the game renders more pixels," which matters for any future fix attempt.

**Resolved this pass (see the resolving finding above): 1920x1080 tracks a real, saved `r_mode` config value, not a hardcoded engine constant** — the earlier open question in this bullet is settled. Two narrower questions remain genuinely open and are NOT blockers for Feature 2 (both are about the stretch-blit/window-vs-backbuffer relationship this issue also surfaced, a separate matter from whether render resolution itself is controllable):
- Whether the "remaining backbuffer area" framing (2560x1440 backbuffer requested at CreateDevice time vs. 1920x1080 actually rendered into per GetViewport, when `r_mode` is left on a non-native saved value) means the extra backbuffer space is stretch-blitted to fill the window or left unrendered — not determined from log data alone, would need a real screenshot/visual check.
- Whether that stretch-blit step (if it exists) is itself a meaningful contributor to issue #87's residual 1440p-vs-1080p stutter correlation, independent of `r_mode`'s actual value — still an open lead for #87, not for this issue.

**Feature 2 implemented (2026-08-25/26), config-driven, NOT YET LIVE-TESTED.** Real RE first, confirming exactly how `r_mode` is set: `FUN_006798e0` (decompiled in full, `re_notes/ghidra_project/`) registers `r_mode` itself, directly (`FUN_00549310("r_mode", &DAT_021ce94c, iVar5, 0x103, "Direct X resolution mode")`) as a real `dvarEnum` whose valid values are `"%ix%i"` (width x height) strings built from the live `EnumAdapterModes` results — flags `0x103` match `real_settings.h`'s own documented DVAR_LATCHED shape. This registration happens exactly once, from `FUN_0067a320`, at the real `IDirect3D9` interface's own creation (`Direct3DCreate9`) — i.e. well before this project's own `CreateDevice` hook or `WndProc` subclass can ever fire, so it's safe to write `r_mode` from any of this project's existing per-tick hooks. `vanilla_settings_table.h`'s documented `ui_r_mode` is a separate, UI-staged mirror dvar the real Options menu itself writes to — not touched by this feature, which writes the real `r_mode` directly instead (matching `real_settings.h`'s own `SetDvarString` semantics: writes the live value immediately, bypassing UI staging, caller must follow with `vid_restart`).

**REJECTED as the wrong mechanism, 2026-08-26 — crashed twice live.** The `r_mode`+`vid_restart` approach above was live-tested and crashed the game both times (once immediately at the first `InjectMenuInputTick` call, once again after adding a 10s startup delay — ruling out startup-timing as the cause). Root cause never fully confirmed (candidates: `r_mode` being a `dvarEnum` written via the generic `SetDvarString` wrapper, which `vanilla_settings_table.h` had already flagged as untested against this specific dvar; or `vid_restart`'s real device-teardown/recreate path being incompatible with this project's own live MinHook detours on `EndScene`/`Reset`/`CreateTexture`) — moot, because the whole approach is now abandoned per direct user redirection: **"thats not doing what i asked, i asked for internal pre scaled render res, we know it scales up from 1080p so"**. The user's real ask was never a display-mode/`vid_restart` change at all — it's a request to control the render resolution WITHIN an unchanged window/backbuffer, the same "engine already renders smaller than the backbuffer and stretches" behavior this issue's own original measurement (`GetViewport`=1920x1080 inside a 2560x1440 backbuffer, `vid_restart` never having fired) already showed happens by default. The `r_mode`/`vid_restart` code path (`ApplyInternalRenderScaleIfConfigured`, `mod_config.cpp`/`.h`) is reverted to inert (config default 0, unchanged from ship default) and should NOT be resumed or further debugged — a different mechanism (below) is the real path forward.

### Real per-frame viewport call chain, traced 2026-08-26 (static RE, `re_notes/ghidra_project/`) — confirms the "smaller viewport than backbuffer" mechanism is real and reusable, exact live-poke target NOT yet nailed down

Traced the actual D3D9 `SetViewport`/`SetScissorRect` call chain from the real vtable dispatch site, confirming this engine genuinely has its own internal "render into a region smaller/larger than the backbuffer" pipeline, independent of `r_mode`/`vid_restart`/device recreation:

- **`FUN_004ab510`** (found via a whole-binary scan for the compiler's real `MOV reg,[base+0xbc]` → `CALL reg` pattern, i.e. the split load-then-call form of a COM vtable dispatch, since a raw fused `CALL [reg+0xbc]` never appears anywhere in the binary — the direct-call scan came back with zero hits, the load-then-call scan found exactly one) is the real, single wrapper that calls both `IDirect3DDevice9::SetViewport` (vtable+0xbc, confirmed against this project's own already-verified vtable offsets for `EndScene`=0xA8/`Reset`=0x40/`CreateTexture`=0x5C, same index arithmetic) and `IDirect3DDevice9::SetScissorRect` (vtable+0x12C/300) back to back, copying a local 4-int (X,Y,W,H) block from a caller-supplied struct pointer before the `SetViewport` call.
- **`FUN_004a2a30`** is a real "set-viewport-if-changed" dedup wrapper: compares an incoming 4-int (X,Y,W,H) rect against a cached copy at a persistent renderer-state global (`DAT_028046e0`, offsets +0xb34/+0xb38/+0xb3c/+0xb40 for the cached X/Y/W/H, +0xc0 for the live `IDirect3DDevice9*`), and only calls `FUN_004ab510` (the real D3D9 call) if the incoming rect actually differs — meaning the real SetViewport call is skipped entirely on frames where nothing changed, not re-issued every single frame regardless.
- **`FUN_004e5b30`** computes the (X,Y,W,H) rect fed into the above, from a second persistent renderer-state global (`DAT_02802f60`): if `*(DAT_02802f60+0x1720) == 1` (the common/default branch), the rect is `{0, 0, *(DAT_02802f60+0x1764), *(DAT_02802f60+0x1768)}` — i.e. **a full-region viewport sized directly from two fields of this global, re-read every time this function runs**, not a one-time snapshot baked into the rect computation itself. The `else` branch (`+0x1720 != 1`) instead uses a *different* 4 fields (`+0x174c/+0x1750/+0x1754/+0x1758`), evidently a genuinely separate sub-rect path (untraced this pass — candidate for split-screen or a letterboxed mode, not yet confirmed).
- **`FUN_004c2710`**, called immediately after `FUN_004a2a30` applies the rect, computes real UV/texture-coordinate scale-and-offset floats (stored at `DAT_02802f60`+0xfb0/0xfb4/0xfb8/0xfbc/0x1270/0x1274/0x1280/0x1284) using `1.0/(DAT_02802f60+0x1764)` and `1.0/(DAT_02802f60+0x1768)` as the reference resolution — **the same two fields that fed the viewport rect above**, confirming these two DWORDs are read as "the reference render resolution" by more than one consumer, not a single-purpose field.
- All three (`FUN_004e5b30` → `FUN_004a2a30` → `FUN_004c2710`) are called together as a fixed triple, gated behind a dirty/pending-resize flag (`*(param+6000) != 0` in three of the four call sites found; a different flag, `DAT_028046d0`, in the fourth), from four distinct call sites (`FUN_006989b0`, `FUN_004aae60`, `FUN_0054ae80`, `FUN_0049bf50`) — none of these four callers were traced further this pass (who calls THEM, and how often per frame, is the actual remaining go/no-go question, see below).
- **The two underlying width/height fields, `DAT_02802f60+0x1764`/`+0x1768` (real absolute addresses `0x028046C4`/`0x028046C8`), have exactly ONE writer anywhere in the binary: `FUN_00694130`**, a real "resize/reallocate render targets" function (memsets two large buffers, `0x200` and `0x800` bytes, then calls a resource-allocation function, `FUN_0047f710`) — confirming these fields are genuinely tied to a render-target-resize event, not just read once at startup and never touched again. `FUN_00694130` does a straight, unconditional copy: `DAT_028046c4 = DAT_024bf4b4; DAT_028046c8 = DAT_024bf4b8` — i.e. it copies from a THIRD pair of globals rather than computing the width/height itself.
- **Not resolved this pass, the actual remaining question**: no writer to `DAT_024bf4b4`/`DAT_024bf4b8` (the ultimate source) was found via a direct-reference scan — only one read site (inside `FUN_00694130` itself) turned up. This means either (a) they're written via a bulk `memcpy`/`memmove` whose destination is computed at runtime rather than a literal matching this exact address, which a direct-reference scan can't see, or (b) they're populated by data outside this binary's own code (loader-initialized, or written by the real d3d9.dll/OS during `CreateDevice`/`Reset` in a way this project hasn't traced). Given `FUN_00694130`'s own name-shape ("resize render targets") and its two big `memset` calls, the leading hypothesis is that `DAT_024bf4b4`/`DAT_024bf4b8` are a cached copy of the real backbuffer/adapter-mode dimensions from `CreateDevice`'s presentation parameters (i.e. WINDOW/backbuffer size, matching this issue's own confirmed 2560x1440 `CreateDevice` diagnostic) — which would mean the "smaller than backbuffer" 1920x1080 viewport this issue originally measured must be coming from the `else` branch of `FUN_004e5b30` (the untraced `+0x174c/1750/1754/1758` sub-rect fields) rather than the `+0x1764/1768` fields this pass focused on. **This is the real, most likely explanation for why the two candidate reference-resolution fields didn't confirm "1920x1080" — they may simply be the wrong field**, and the untraced sub-rect fields are the actual next lead, not yet chased.

**Consequence / honest status**: this pass confirms, with real decompiled evidence, that the engine's `SetViewport` call chain is genuinely dedup'd, dirty-flag-gated, and driven by re-readable persistent globals rather than a value baked in once at device creation — strong circumstantial support for "a live poke to the right global, without touching `r_mode`/`vid_restart`/the device at all, could work." But the EXACT field to poke is not yet nailed down: `DAT_02802f60+0x1764/+0x1768` were the most obvious candidate and got fully traced to their single writer, but that writer's own source (`DAT_024bf4b4/+b8`) could not be traced further this pass, and circumstantial evidence now points toward those two fields tracking window/backbuffer size (not the smaller "1920x1080" viewport this issue is actually chasing) rather than being the render-resolution control point itself. **Do not implement a live poke against `DAT_02802f60+0x1764/+0x1768` yet** — the untraced `else`-branch sub-rect fields (`DAT_02802f60+0x174c/+0x1750/+0x1754/+0x1758`) and the four `FUN_004e5b30` call sites (who calls `FUN_006989b0`/`FUN_004aae60`/`FUN_0054ae80`/`FUN_0049bf50`, and how often per frame) are the real next steps, not yet done. This is genuine, real progress (a confirmed, safe-looking mechanism class exists) but not yet a confirmed, ready-to-implement hook target — matching this project's own "no placeholder hooks, no guessed offsets" standard, this stops at documented findings, no implementation this pass.

Implemented: new `[Video] InternalRenderScalePercent` config key (`mod_config.h`/`.cpp`, config schema v21→v22), 0=disabled (default) or a percentage of the real desktop native resolution (`GetSystemMetrics(SM_CXSCREEN/SM_CYSCREEN)`). 100 is guaranteed valid (the current desktop resolution is always a real enumerated adapter mode); other percentages are best-effort since this project has no way to read the engine's own enumerated mode list back from C++. Applied once per process from `InjectMenuInputTick` (`ApplyInternalRenderScaleIfConfigured()`, `mod_config.cpp`) via `SetDvarString("r_mode", ...)` + `QueueConsoleCommand("vid_restart\n")`, logged (target resolution, immediate pre-restart readback). Deliberately NOT re-applied on config hot-reload — requires a game restart, same as any other DVAR_LATCHED setting. Real motivation, direct user framing: fixing a stuck legacy-`r_mode`-default softness on >1080p displays ("above 1080p it looks bad like 2005 bad"), not primarily a performance-downscale tool, though the same mechanism supports that direction too.

**Builds clean per the fork that implemented it (not independently re-verified by the coordinator this pass — host build/verification still pending). NOT YET LIVE-TESTED**: whether `vid_restart` actually recreates the D3D9 device cleanly under this project's own hooks (does the proxy survive it, do controller/overlay hooks reattach correctly) has not been run. ### Untraced sub-rect fields resolved, 2026-08-26, second parallel pass (static RE, `re_notes/ghidra_project/`) — the exact chain traces to a ONE-SHOT startup computation, not a per-frame one; the go/no-go from the pass above is now answered differently than its own framing assumed

Ran in parallel with the pass immediately above, chasing exactly the item it flagged as still open ("the untraced `else`-branch sub-rect fields `DAT_02802f60+0x174c/+0x1750/+0x1754/+0x1758`"). Resolved fully via `FindDataWriters.java`/`FindCallers.java` against `re_notes/ghidra_project/`:

- **`DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` (the reference W/H feeding that sub-rect) have exactly ONE writer: `FUN_00679010`**, a real, fully decompiled "resolution quality-tier clamp" function. It takes a struct pointer (custom register-passed convention — not resolvable from the decompiler's C alone, matching this binary's established pattern for functions like this one) with real fields at `+0x1c`/`+0x20` (a requested width/height) and `+0x24`/`+0x28` (an upper-bound width/height, almost certainly the real native/backbuffer size). It clamps the requested value into a quality tier (`0x500x0x2d0`/`0x640x??`/`0x780x??` depending on an aspect-ratio comparison against real float constants), re-clamps against the upper bound, and sets a real "is this actually scaled" flag (`DAT_021d2e18` = 0 if the clamped result exactly equals the upper bound, 1 otherwise). **This is, functionally, the internal pre-scaled render resolution computation this feature is chasing.**
- **`FUN_00679010` has exactly ONE caller, `FUN_00679db0`**, which calls it, then `FUN_00463820` (the sub-rect writer) immediately after, then several other real subsystem calls, then conditionally `FUN_00469350` (the other sub-rect writer/big reset) further down — confirming `FUN_00679db0` is the real, single "commit a (re)computed resolution" pipeline.
- **`FUN_00679db0` has exactly ONE caller: `FUN_0067a320`** — already known in this project's history (this issue's earlier pass: the function where `Direct3DCreate9` is called, and where `r_mode`'s own registration, `FUN_006798e0`, happens immediately after). Full decompile confirms `FUN_0067a320` is a genuine ONE-SHOT startup orchestrator: it early-returns if `DAT_021cd928 != 0` (already-initialized guard), otherwise runs `Direct3DCreate9` once, `FUN_006798e0` once, then a `do{...}while(true)` display-mode-selection retry loop that calls `FUN_00679db0` — meaning the entire W/H-computation chain above runs **exactly once per process, at real startup**, well before this project's own `CreateDevice` hook can fire.

**Real conclusion, resolving the parallel pass's open question with a different answer than its own framing assumed**: the render resolution is NOT recomputed live every frame or on `Reset` — it is computed exactly ONCE at real startup, via a clean, fully single-path-traced chain: `FUN_0067a320` → `FUN_00679db0` → `FUN_00679010` (computes the clamped W/H into `DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c`) → `FUN_00463820` (copies that into the actual sub-rect, `DAT_02802f60+0x174c..58`, that the per-frame `SetViewport` dedup chain from the pass above reads every call). This means the pass above's own "does this fire once per frame or on rare resize" question doesn't actually need answering to implement the feature — the SOURCE value is set once, and the per-frame chain just keeps re-reading that same already-computed rect every call (dedup'd, so `SetViewport` itself is only reissued when it changes, but the underlying number is startup-fixed either way).

**This is real, materially good news for the feature**: the safe hook point is a ONE-SHOT startup hook on `FUN_00679010` (or immediately after its single call site inside `FUN_00679db0`) that overrides the computed `DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` (clamped to the real upper-bound fields the function itself already reads) before `FUN_00463820` consumes them a few instructions later in the same caller — entirely inside the engine's own existing, always-executed startup path. **Zero interaction with `r_mode`, zero `vid_restart`, zero device/window recreation** — a materially lower-risk mechanism than the rejected approach earlier in this issue, since nothing about device/window lifetime is touched at all.

**Root cause, found via direct RE follow-up** (the same session, static Ghidra RE against `re_notes/ghidra_project/`, real vtable-dispatch scans for `SetRenderTarget`(0x94)/`CreateRenderTarget`(0x70) and real decompiles of every hit):

- `FUN_00542cb0` is the ONLY real `SetRenderTarget` call site in the binary.
- `FUN_00682d70` -- one level up the render-target-creation chain -- calls the real `CreateRenderTarget` (vtable 0x70) using `DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` (the exact pair the abandoned attempt overrode) as width/height, but the surface it creates is explicitly named via a real localized string: `R_RENDERTARGET_SAVED_SCREEN`. This is a SECONDARY buffer, not the primary scene target.
- Its own caller chain (`FUN_00682d70`/`FUN_00682e50` -> `FUN_00682fa0` -> `FUN_00683060`, all fully decompiled) allocates the REAL scene/post-processing pipeline -- `R_RENDERTARGET_RESOLVED_SCENE`, `R_RENDERTARGET_FLOAT_Z`, `R_RENDERTARGET_SSAO`/`SSAO_BLURRED`/`SSAO_FLOAT_Z`, `R_RENDERTARGET_POST_EFFECT_0`/`1`, `R_RENDERTARGET_PINGPONG_0`/`1` -- and EVERY ONE of these real `CreateRenderTarget` calls is sized from a COMPLETELY DIFFERENT pair, `DAT_021d2e00`/`DAT_021d2e04` (or a half/quarter-scaled derivative of it for the SSAO/post-effect/pingpong buffers specifically).
- Full decompile of `FUN_00679010` (the function that writes both pairs) makes the relationship exact: `DAT_021d2e00 = *(param_1+0x1c); DAT_021d2e04 = *(param_1+0x20);` -- a DIRECT, COMPLETELY UNCLAMPED copy of the function's own REQUESTED W/H input. `DAT_021d2e08`/`0c` (what the abandoned attempt overrode) is a SEPARATE, tier-clamped value (discrete steps 1280/1600/1920, capped to native) computed independently in the same function, feeding ONLY `SAVED_SCREEN`.
- **Conclusion: the abandoned `FUN_00463820` hook only ever changed a screenshot/thumbnail buffer's reported size and the metadata `GetViewport` happened to echo back -- it never touched the real scene render target or any real GPU-visible surface at all.** This fully explains the "no FPS change" report: the real `RESOLVED_SCENE`/post-effect chain was allocated at its ORIGINAL, unmodified size the entire time.

**Real fix, implemented same session**: `Hook_FUN_00679010` (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`) replaces `Hook_FUN_00463820` entirely (fully removed, not left disabled). It hooks `FUN_00679010` itself as a PRE-hook -- confirmed via raw disassembly to take a genuine single-argument fastcall convention (`this` in ECX only, no stack args), directly expressible in MSVC as `void(__fastcall*)(void*)` with no naked-asm trampoline needed. Before calling the real trampoline, if `InternalRenderScalePercent > 0`, it overwrites the struct's own REQUESTED W/H fields (`+0x1c`/`+0x20`) with a target computed from the REAL native/upper-bound fields on the same struct (`+0x24`/`+0x28`, read live, not cached), floor-clamped to the engine's own real 640x480 minimum, with **no ceiling clamp against native** -- since `DAT_021d2e00`/`04` never clamps against native either, this is what actually enables genuine supersampling above 100%.

**Timing, also corrected**: `FUN_00679010` has exactly one real caller (`FUN_00679db0`), itself called exactly once from `FUN_0067a320`'s real device-creation path -- confirmed via decompile that `FUN_0067a320` has its own early-return guard (`if (DAT_021cd928 != 0) { ...; return; }`) proving its creation path never re-runs on a later call. Unlike the abandoned `FUN_00463820` attempt (wrongly believed to fire continuously; it does not -- all 4 of its own real callers are lifecycle/event-driven, not per-frame, a claim from the section above that also needed correcting), this hook fires exactly ONCE per process. **A config change now requires a full game restart, not a hot-reload** -- there is no live-apply path, since the real render targets are only ever created once. This is still strictly safer than both prior attempts: no live device teardown/recreate ever happens, `r_mode`/`vid_restart` are never touched, and the one-shot nature is a direct, unavoidable consequence of intercepting a genuinely one-time engine computation, not an artificial limitation.

**Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors), `d3d9.dll` redeployed with a fresh timestamp.**

**Status: RESOLVED, confirmed live under the correct mechanism (2026-08-26).** Fresh restart with `InternalRenderScalePercent=300` on the same 2560x1440 native display: **220fps at 100%, 70-80fps at 300%** -- real, expected GPU cost scaling (9x pixel count producing a real, proportionate frame-cost increase), the exact missing signal that caught the prior attempt's bug in the first place. This is genuine, confirmed-working proof the override now reaches real GPU-visible render targets, not just reported metadata. Feature is DONE for its original scope (internal render resolution control, fixing sub-native softness and enabling real supersampling) -- no further work planned on this specific mechanism unless a new bug is reported.

## 89. Survival scoreboard: real stat data source -- CONFIRMED (GSC script-local state, not natively readable), real policy checkpoint now applies (2026-08-25)

**Status: RESOLVED (the RE question), and CLOSED for the main mod -- deferred to the plugin API instead (see the Decision entry below).** The real data source is now definitively known, straight from the actual decompiled GSC source (see below) -- every value the between-round summary shows lives in per-player GSC script-local associative-array fields (`self._id_18D3[...]`), not a dvar, not a native entity-struct field, not anything this project's existing C++ code has any established way to read. Per this project's own standing policy (`CODE_STANDARDS.md`'s Input Validation & Security section), reading live GSC-VM/entity script state is explicitly the class of thing requiring its own separate go/no-go conversation with the user -- this entry stops at reporting the real finding, it does not propose or design a read.

**Direct user follow-up, same day: "do the gsc lookup didnt we already decomp it for inspection"** -- correct, and a real miss in the two prior passes on this issue: `re_notes/survival_mode_overview.md` (an EARLIER session, 2026-07-18) already had this scriptfile identified and partially summarized, and the actual decompiled source was still sitting on disk at `D:\Tools\gsc-tool\extracted\decompiled\iw5\1571.gsc` (2183 lines, `xensik/gsc-tool`'s own real output) the whole time -- neither of the two forks that worked this issue found or checked either the existing summary doc or the existing decompiled file before doing their own from-scratch native-binary searches. A real, avoidable "checking is far cheaper than digging" miss (`CODE_STANDARDS.md`'s own standard) -- an existing-file search by name/topic should happen before dispatching new RE work, not after.

**Goal**: find where Survival's between-round summary screen ("Combat Performance", "Wave Bonus: $X", "Accuracy:", "Headshots", "Damage Taken:") gets its real numeric values from, as the prerequisite RE step for a live Survival scoreboard feature (bound to Back, styled like the custom Options screen, PREVIEW/WIP off by default -- see the approved plan for the full feature scope).

**What was tried**: a real, exact-string Ghidra search for the literal captured text ("Combat Performance", "Accuracy:", etc.) came back with ZERO hits in `iw5sp.exe` -- these strings are NOT baked into the exe as raw C strings. Consistent with this project's own already-established finding elsewhere (issue #68, the language pass) that this engine's real UI text is localized, resolved from `.str` reference keys at runtime, not hardcoded English. A follow-up substring search for lowercase GSC-field-name-shaped tokens (`damagetaken`, `accuracy`, `kills`, `combat`, `wave`) DID find real hits -- but tracing their cross-references led to a single, shared function, `FUN_00470d00`, confirmed via decompile to be the game's own **master GSC string-intern table**: a huge (~600-entry) function that interns hundreds of unrelated GSC field/event names used throughout the ENTIRE game (AI behavior fields, weapon tags, vehicle fields, arbitrary HUD-element properties like `label`/`color`/`alignx`, all in the same table). A real, confirmed finding, but a false lead for this specific purpose -- it only proves these words exist as *some* GSC-exposed field somewhere in the whole codebase, not that they're specifically this screen's own data source. A dvar-naming-convention shortcut search (`player_kills`, `sv_survival_*`-shaped names) found nothing relevant either (only Survival map names, e.g. `survival_mp_paris`).

**Real conclusion**: the between-round summary's actual values are very likely populated by the compiled Survival gamemode's own GSC scriptfile (setting a HUD element's real field via the same interned strings found above -- `label`/`color`/`alignx` sitting in that exact intern table alongside `accuracy`/`kills`/`damagetaken` strongly suggests a scripted HUD-creation call, not an exe-side dvar), which a binary string/xref search alone cannot resolve. **The real next step is actual GSC bytecode decompilation** of the Survival gamemode scriptfile -- this project already has `xensik/gsc-tool` set up (per `CLAUDE.md`'s Stack section, carried over from earlier GSC work) for exactly this. Not attempted this pass -- a separate, larger RE task than a binary string search covers, genuinely deferred, not abandoned.

**Consequence for the scoreboard feature**: UI implementation (3b in the approved plan) cannot start with real data yet -- the RE step (3a) needs a real GSC decompile pass first. Do not build placeholder/fake numbers into the UI in the meantime; per this project's own Production-Ready Only standard, a UI shell with no real data source behind it is not a step toward "done," it's exactly the kind of half-finished work this project's standards explicitly reject.

**Follow-up pass, same day: real, concrete evidence for WHY a native-side search can't find this.** A pre-existing Ghidra project for `iw5sp.exe` was found at `D:\Tools\ghidra_projects_survivalscore\` (`MW3.gpr`) -- worth reusing for any future RE pass on this binary instead of standing up a new project each time. Using it, located and decompiled the real entity-field GETTER dispatcher, `FUN_00613d10` -- a genuine, confirmed field-name dispatch table (string-compares a requested field name against `teamname`, `clipAmmo`, `stockAmmo`, `fragAmmo`, `score`, `deaths`, `kills`, `number`, and more, calling a real native getter function per match). **`score`, `deaths`, and `kills` ARE recognized as valid field names in this dispatcher, but have NO real getter wired up in this SP binary** -- the decompiled control flow shows all three (along with one unresolved symbol) fall straight through to `*outType = 0; *outValue = 0; return;` with no actual data lookup, unlike every other field in the same table (`clipAmmo`/`stockAmmo`/`fragAmmo`/`nightvision`/etc.), each of which calls a real native function. Only `number` (further down the same chain) reaches a real getter (`FUN_004b14a0`). Two other candidate functions from the earlier pass's own XREF list (`FUN_005d9a30`, `FUN_005ce040`) were checked and ruled out -- both are unrelated GSC animscript-table registration helpers (`GScr_SetScriptAndLabel`-shaped), the same class of false lead as the shared string-intern table found in the original pass.

**Real conclusion, now with concrete supporting evidence**: `self.kills`/`self.score`/`self.deaths` -- the obvious native GSC entity fields a scoreboard would want -- are confirmed non-functional stubs in `iw5sp.exe`, most likely because they're genuinely MP-scoreboard-shaped fields sharing the same compiled entity-field system as SP, but never wired to real data there. This means Survival's real kill/score/death-adjacent stats CANNOT be coming from the standard native entity-field getters at all -- they must be tracked entirely in GSC script-local state (`level`/`self` script variables the compiled Survival gamemode script maintains itself), invisible to any native-side dispatcher search no matter how thorough.

**CONFIRMED via the actual decompiled GSC source, `1571.gsc` (`D:\Tools\gsc-tool\extracted\decompiled\iw5\1571.gsc`, lines 173-214) -- the exact function that populates the between-round summary UI:**

```
foreach ( var_8 in level.players )
{
    var_9  = var_8._id_18D3["kill"];        var_10 = _id_3F6A( var_8, "kill" );
    var_11 = var_8._id_18D3["headshot"];    var_12 = _id_3F6A( var_8, "headshot" );
    var_13 = var_8._id_18D3["accuracy"] + "%";  var_14 = _id_3F6A( var_8, "accuracy" );
    var_15 = var_8._id_18D3["credits"];     var_16 = _id_3F6A( var_8, "credits" );
    var_17 = var_8._id_18D3["downed"];      var_18 = _id_3F6A( var_8, "downed" );
    var_19 = var_8._id_18D3["revives"];     var_20 = _id_3F6A( var_8, "revives" );
    ...
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_KILLS", var_9, var_10 );
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_HEADSHOT", var_11, var_12 );
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_ACCURACY", var_13, var_14 );
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_REVIVES", var_19, var_20 );
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_CREDITS_EARNED", var_15, var_16 );
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_TIME", var_5 );          // formatted elapsed time
    var_8 maps\_utility::_id_16C7( "@SO_SURVIVAL_PERFORMANCE_SCORE", var_6 );         // var_6 = _id_3F69()
}
```

Every single stat on the summary screen -- kills, headshots, accuracy, credits earned, downed count, revives -- reads from `self._id_18D3["<key>"]`, a per-player GSC associative-array field maintained entirely by the Survival gamemode script itself (`_id_3F93()`/the surrounding wave-completion logic, same file, lines ~1125-1420, already independently confirmed the ACCUMULATION side of this: `self._id_18D3["headshot"]++` on a `sur_ch_headshot` notify, `self._id_18D3["accuracy"] = clamp(100*hits/shotsFired, 0, 100)`, `self._id_18D3["damagetaken"] += <amount>`, etc.). Total `SCORE` comes from a separate helper, `_id_3F69()`, not yet traced further. The wave-bonus dollar formula is also now fully known: `bonus = headshots*W_hs - max(accuracy-25,0)*W_acc - damagetaken*W_dmg`, with per-difficulty weights `level._id_3F94["headshot"]` (50 or 20), `["accuracy"]`=3, `["damagetaken"]`=2 (lines 1125-1419).

**This is GSC script-VM state, not a dvar and not a native C struct field -- there is no established, already-safe way for this project's own C++ code to read it.** `self._id_18D3[...]` is a dynamic, script-managed associative array living entirely inside the GSC VM's own per-entity variable storage, a fundamentally different (and, if anything, MORE invasive) class of read than the live gameplay-entity-memory reads this project's aim-assist removal already drew a hard line against (`known_issues.md` issue #33, `CODE_STANDARDS.md`'s Input Validation & Security section: "the decision to read entity/world memory AT ALL is a separate, explicit go/no-go conversation with the user every time, not something this standard pre-authorizes"). **This entry does not propose or design a read of this data** -- it stops here, at reporting the real, now-fully-confirmed source, exactly as the approved plan's own Feature 3a section anticipated this outcome and specified this stopping point in advance.

**Consequence for the Survival scoreboard feature as originally scoped**: the feature cannot be built the way it was planned (a live overlay showing real per-player Survival stats) without either (a) an explicit go/no-go conversation and decision to read GSC-VM state specifically, which this entry does not make on its own, or (b) a fundamentally different, narrower scope that doesn't need this data at all. Genuinely blocked pending that conversation -- not a "keep digging" situation, the RE question itself is now fully answered.

**Decision (2026-08-25, same day): deferred to the plugin API, not built into the main mod.** Direct user framing: "even sp that poses a risk possible deferrence to plugin." ## 90. 60fps engine tick: com_maxfps/fixedtime/com_timescale CONFIRMED real, registered, and clustered -- fixedtime's real mechanism now DECOMPILED and confirmed (2026-08-25)

**Status: Investigating -- `fixedtime`'s own mechanism and call cadence now fully decompiled and confirmed; the actual downstream 30Hz-gating mechanism (issue #87/#79's own confirmed alternating-frame-cost evidence) is still NOT located, so the plan's core go/no-go question remains genuinely open.** `com_maxfps` stays ruled out (see correction below). No live patch attempted -- this remains static RE only, per the approved plan's own "static RE first, explicit go/no-go before patching" bar.

**Goal**: determine whether `iw5sp.exe`'s locked 30Hz simulation tick (already established via real `frametime_benchmark.csv` evidence, issue #87/#79) is a single, cleanly-patchable value, as the prerequisite RE step for an opt-in, SP-only 60fps engine tick feature (see the approved plan for full scope -- `iw5sp.exe` only, never `iw5mp.exe`, VAC-risk-motivated).

**Method**: parsed `iw5sp.exe`'s real PE section table directly (no ASLR, confirmed elsewhere in this project's docs -- ImageBase 0x00400000 always) to compute each candidate string's real virtual address, then searched the WHOLE file for 4-byte little-endian occurrences of that VA -- the byte pattern a `push offset stringName` x86 instruction produces. This directly answers "is this string ever loaded as an operand anywhere in the code," a real (if blunt) substitute for Ghidra's own cross-reference view, and already caught this project's own precedent for a dead-string false lead (`ai_nosight`, zero XREFs) the same way, so a nonzero-XREF result here carries real weight, not just string presence.

**Findings**:
- `com_maxfps`: exactly 1 real XREF, file offset `0x206D51`, VA `0x00607951`. Raw bytes immediately preceding: `6a 00 6a 00 68 38 2e 85 00` -- `push 0; push 0; push offset com_maxfps` (VA `0x00852E38`), i.e. a genuine 3-argument call setup, the same shape this project's own prior sessions have already confirmed for real dvar-registration calls (`g_ai`, `timescale`).
- `fixedtime`: exactly 1 real XREF, file offset `0x206E20`, VA `0x00607A20` -- only `0xCF` (207) bytes after `com_maxfps`'s own registration site, same `push 0; push 0; push offset fixedtime` shape.
- `com_timescale`: exactly 1 real XREF, file offset `0x206DD1`, VA `0x006079D1` -- sits BETWEEN the other two (roughly halfway), same call shape. `com_timescale` is very likely the real underlying dvar behind this project's own already-shipped, confirmed-working F2 debug-freeze feature (bare `"timescale"` itself has ZERO real XREFs anywhere in the file -- present as a string but never loaded as an operand, meaning the F2 feature's real dvar is `com_timescale`, and the bare `"timescale"` string is a red herring/unrelated leftover, not the one this project's own existing code actually depends on -- worth double-checking the F2 feature's own source comment against this, since it may currently misdescribe which literal dvar name it targets even though the FEATURE itself demonstrably works).
- All three registration sites fall within a single, tight ~0x150-byte window (`0x206D00`-`0x206E50`) of raw executable code, containing a clearly repeating `push 0; push 0; push offset <string>; call <rel32>` pattern several times over (visible directly in the raw hex dump, not just for these 3 strings) -- strong circumstantial evidence this is one shared, batch "register client frame-timing dvars" initialization function, not three unrelated call sites that happen to share a shape.

**Not yet done, real next step**: get an actual Ghidra project stood up for `iw5sp.exe` (none existed) and headless- or GUI-decompile the function containing `0x206D00`-`0x206E50` in full -- name it, confirm its real callers (is it a one-time init, called from `iw5sp.exe`'s own real client-startup path?), and trace what `com_maxfps`'s own registered `dvar_t*` is actually READ by elsewhere in the binary (a genuinely different, harder search than confirming registration -- the dvar's VALUE gets read via a pointer/handle returned by the registration call, not by referencing the name string again, so this needs real decompilation of the registration call's return value usage, not another raw-byte string search). That read site is what actually answers whether raising `com_maxfps` changes real simulation cadence or just render/frame-submission rate -- genuinely unknown until that's found.

**Consequence for the 60fps-tick feature**: real, promising groundwork laid (this is NOT a dead string the way `ai_nosight` was), but the actual go/no-go question from the approved plan ("is this a small, contained patch or does 30Hz assumption appear baked into multiple separate places") is still open. Do not attempt any live patch based on this pass alone -- registration existing is necessary but not sufficient evidence that a value change would produce a correct, stable 60Hz simulation.

**CORRECTION (2026-08-25, same day, direct user framing): "com maxfps is just the console option to limit frames from all cods, thats not internal engine sim rate."** Correct, and this was a real miss in the writeup above -- `com_maxfps` is the standard idTech/CoD-family CLIENT RENDER-RATE limiter, the same mechanism every CoD title has had since Quake3, structurally unrelated to the fixed simulation-tick cadence. This project's own already-established evidence (issue #87/#79's real `frametime_benchmark.csv` capture) already proves the two are decoupled in THIS binary specifically: the render loop ran freely at ~200fps uncapped while the simulation-tied cost pattern stayed locked to a real 30Hz cadence underneath it -- direct, existing proof `com_maxfps` (or the absence of any cap) does NOT change simulation rate, since if it did, an uncapped/high `com_maxfps` at 200fps would have produced 200Hz-cadence simulation cost, not the confirmed 30Hz pattern. **`com_maxfps` is therefore NOT a real candidate for this feature and should not be chased further as one** -- confirming it's a genuinely registered dvar (true, and still useful as proof this project's own XREF methodology works on this binary) does not make it relevant to sim-tick rate.

**Real remaining candidates, in priority order for the next pass**: `fixedtime` is the much stronger lead of the two remaining -- a genuine idTech/Quake3-family term specifically for forcing a FIXED time delta into the simulation step each frame (used historically for demo recording/frame-perfect debugging, not a player-facing setting), a structurally different and much more directly relevant mechanism than a render-rate cap. Decompile `fixedtime`'s own consuming logic first, not `com_maxfps`'s. Independent of any of these three dvars, the original plan's own step 2 (trace `FUN_0057de60`/`FUN_0057e480`, the already-found real per-frame simulation-stepping functions, directly for wherever the fixed ~33.33ms cadence between steps is actually enforced) remains the more reliable path regardless of dvar findings, since a hardcoded constant with no dvar backing at all is a real possibility this project's own history has already seen before (`ai_nosight` was a registered-but-dead dvar; the reverse -- a hardcoded value with NO dvar at all gating it -- is equally plausible and wouldn't show up in any string-based search no matter how thorough).

### Real decompile pass (2026-08-25, same day, continuation) -- fixedtime's actual consuming logic found and confirmed

**A Ghidra project for `iw5sp.exe` was stood up this pass** (`re_notes/ghidra_project/`, headless import + full auto-analysis via `analyzeHeadless.bat`, ~124s) -- none existed before. This project's own existing headless RE scripts (`re_notes/ghidra_scripts/FuncAtAddr.java`, `DecompileFuncs.java`, `FindGlobalRefs.java`) were reused directly, no new tooling needed.

**`FUN_00607940` (the dvar-registration function found last pass at VA `0x00607940`, containing `com_maxfps`/`fixedtime`/`com_timescale`'s registration calls) fully decompiled.** Confirms ALL of: `com_maxfps`, `sys_lockThreads`, `sys_smp_allowed`, `com_timescale` ("Scale time of each frame"), **bare `timescale`** ("Scale time of each frame" -- a SEPARATE, independently-registered dvar, own call site, own storage global `DAT_0176b530`), `fixedtime` ("Use a fixed time rate for each frame"), `com_maxFrameTime` ("Time slows down if a frame takes longer than this many milliseconds"), `cl_paused`, `sv_running`, plus ~15 unrelated dvars (bandwidth caps, UI flags) all in one shared client-init registration block.

**CORRECTION to last pass's own claim that bare `timescale` has zero real XREFs**: wrong -- the earlier raw-byte VA cross-reference search missed it (likely a compiler/string-table layout quirk the blunter byte-search technique couldn't handle correctly). The real decompile shows `timescale` IS independently registered (`FUN_004f9cc0("timescale",0x3f800000,...)`, its own storage global `DAT_0176b530`, separate from `com_timescale`'s own `DAT_01769f38`) -- this project's own existing F2 debug-freeze feature description does NOT need correcting after all; both dvars are real, and which one the F2 feature actually reads was not re-verified this pass (out of scope -- that feature already works, not broken, just worth noting the earlier "correction" claim about it was itself wrong). Lesson: a real Ghidra decompile is not always replaceable by a faster raw-byte substitute, even one that worked correctly for other strings in the same pass.

**`FUN_004aa1a0` -- the real per-frame time-delta computation function, found via `FindGlobalRefs.java` (the one function touching `fixedtime`+`com_timescale`+`timescale` together) -- fully decompiled, CONCLUSIVE:**
```c
float10 FUN_004aa1a0(void)
{
  if (*(int *)(DAT_01769f2c + 0xc) != 0) {          // fixedtime's registered int value != 0
    return (float10)*(int *)(DAT_01769f2c + 0xc);    // return fixedtime's raw value DIRECTLY as the frame time
  }
  return (float10)(*(float *)(DAT_0176b530 + 0xc) * *(float *)(DAT_01769f38 + 0xc));
  // else: normal path -- timescale * com_timescale (the two multiplier dvars)
}
```
**This directly, conclusively confirms `fixedtime`'s own registration description ("Use a fixed time rate for each frame") is real and functional, not a dead/leftover dvar.** When set to a nonzero value, this function returns THAT value directly as the effective per-call frame-time delta, completely bypassing the normal timescale-multiplier path.

**`FUN_00607e50` -- the real outer frame-time orchestrator that calls the above -- also decompiled, confirms the SAME fixedtime override propagates into the actual per-frame timing used downstream** (not just a value some unrelated diagnostic reads): checks `fixedtime`'s registered value directly; if set, the function's own return value (the effective elapsed-time-this-frame figure fed onward) becomes `fixedtime`'s configured value instead of a real-elapsed-time-based computation.

**What this means for the 60fps-tick feature, and what's still open**: `fixedtime` is a REAL, working, already-shipped-in-retail native lever for forcing a fixed per-simulated-frame time delta -- not merely a registered-but-unused string. This is genuinely promising: if the function this feeds into is called once per real RENDERED frame (this project's own confirmed-uncapped ~200fps capture, issue #87/#79, shows frames ARE submitted far faster than 30/sec when nothing throttles them), setting `fixedtime` to a small value (e.g. ~16-17, if units are milliseconds as the registration description implies) could plausibly make the simulation advance in smaller, more frequent steps -- closer to a real 60Hz update rate -- PROVIDED render frames are actually being submitted often enough to consume those smaller steps. **Not yet confirmed this pass**: (1) the exact unit of `fixedtime`'s value (milliseconds assumed from context/description, not independently proven), (2) whether `FUN_0057e480`/`FUN_0057de60` (the already-documented per-frame usercmd pipeline) actually consume `FUN_00607e50`'s output on every real render call or on some other cadence, (3) whether ANY of movement integration, animation blend rates, or physics step size elsewhere in the codebase separately assume a 30Hz/33ms cadence independent of this exact function (the original plan's own core go/no-go question) -- this pass traced the TIME-DELTA COMPUTATION mechanism itself, not yet every CONSUMER of that computed delta. **Next step**: trace `FUN_0057e480`/`FUN_0057de60`'s own callers to confirm the real call cadence, and audit movement/animation/physics code for any hardcoded 30Hz/33ms assumption independent of this delta value, before considering a live `fixedtime` test.

Ghidra project preserved at `re_notes/ghidra_project/` for the next pass to reuse (headless import already done, ~124s saved).

### Real decompile pass 2 (2026-08-25, same day, continuation) -- call cadence, unit, and a false lead on the 30Hz mechanism resolved

Reused `re_notes/ghidra_project/` directly, no re-analysis needed. Traced callers upward from `FUN_00607e50` using this project's own existing `FindCallers.java` script.

**Call cadence resolved -- `FUN_00607e50` is called exactly once per iteration of the real main engine loop, uncapped at that level:**
- `FUN_00607e50`'s only caller is `FUN_00458600` (renamed candidate: `Com_Frame`'s inner body). Immediately before calling it, `FUN_00458600` computes `local_4 = (int)(1000 / iVar6)` where `iVar6` is a target-fps value read from a registered dvar (`DAT_0176b540 + 0xc`) -- the classic idTech "convert target FPS into ms-per-frame" throttle computation. This CONFIRMS the unit question directly: this ms-per-frame value feeds the exact same downstream chain `FUN_00607e50`'s own return value feeds (both become `uVar4`/`iVar6` consumed by `FUN_0048b880`("SV_Frame")/`FUN_0052d590` a few lines later) -- so `fixedtime`'s own return value from `FUN_00607e50` (already confirmed pass 1: raw int cast to float) is unambiguously in the **same unit as this computed value: milliseconds**, not seconds or engine ticks. This was "assumed from context" in pass 1; now directly proven by the shared-consumer relationship.
- `FUN_00458600` itself is called from `FUN_0044c7b0`, confirmed via the real diagnostic string `"Com_Frame_Try_Block_Function"` wrapping the call -- this is the genuine `Com_Frame()` entry point.
- `FUN_0044c7b0` is called from `FUN_00534380` (the real WinMain-equivalent -- sets process priority, calls `SteamAPI_RestartAppIfNecessary`, etc.) inside a **tight, unconditional `do { ... FUN_0044c7b0(); } while(true)` loop** -- no `Sleep`, no `WaitMessage`, no explicit frame-rate throttle visible at THIS level. This directly confirms the main loop calls `Com_Frame` (and therefore `FUN_00607e50`/`fixedtime`'s consuming logic) as fast as the OS will schedule it, exactly matching this project's own already-confirmed ~200fps-uncapped `frametime_benchmark.csv` capture (issue #87/#79) -- there is no separate fixed-30Hz *call* gate at the main-loop level. Any throttling to a real target framerate happens via the `1000/iVar6` ms-per-frame value computed just above (almost certainly consumed by a blocking/spin-wait call inside `FUN_00458600` not shown in this trace, structurally the same role `com_maxfps` plays in every idTech3-derived engine) -- NOT via gating how often `Com_Frame` itself is invoked.

**Consequence: `fixedtime` overrides the ELAPSED-TIME VALUE reported per `Com_Frame` call, it does NOT create or control a separate 30Hz call cadence -- the real 30Hz-cost pattern from issue #87/#79 must be enforced somewhere DOWNSTREAM of this value**, inside whatever actually consumes it (most likely `SV_Frame`, confirmed as the real string-identified function `FUN_0048b880` -> `FUN_00424a50`, called directly after `FUN_00607e50` in `FUN_00458600` with that same computed frametime as its argument).

**False lead found and ruled out, documented so it isn't re-chased**: `FUN_00424a50` ("SV_Frame"'s real body) contains `DAT_01deccdc = 0x32 - DAT_01deccb4;` (0x32 = 50 decimal) -- initially looked like a classic idTech3 `sv_fps`-style frame-scheduling accumulator (50ms = 20Hz tick, a very plausible sibling to a 30Hz assumption). **Decompiling the actual consumer, `FUN_0050e020`, disproves this**: the `DAT_01decc*` variable cluster (`DAT_01decccc`, `DAT_01deccd0`, `_DAT_01deccd4`, `DAT_01deccb4`/`DAT_01deccdc`) is a real, but unrelated, **co-op HOST-TIMEOUT accumulator** -- confirmed via the real embedded string `"COOP_HOSTTIMEOUT"` read directly inside `FUN_0050e020`, and its own `0x32` multiplier (`DAT_01deccd0 * 0x32 + DAT_01decccc`) is a host-timeout-window scaling factor, not a per-tick scheduler. This is exactly the kind of coincidental-constant trap this project's own Code Quality Standards already warn about (grep the whole cluster, don't assume a nearby constant is the mechanism you're looking for just because the value matches) -- flagged here so a future pass doesn't waste time re-chasing this specific dead end.

**Still genuinely unresolved (the plan's own core go/no-go question)**: the real mechanism that produces the confirmed 30Hz-alternating-cost pattern (issue #87/#79) has NOT been located. `SV_Frame`'s own top-level branches (`FUN_00424a50`) were traced in full this pass and contain no other obvious msec-accumulator besides the ruled-out coop-timeout one -- the real tick-pacing logic is either (a) inside one of `FUN_00424a50`'s many un-decompiled callees not yet examined (`FUN_004be3f0`, `FUN_00553bd0`, `FUN_00537180`, `FUN_006522b0`, `FUN_004708c0`, `FUN_00465e90`, `FUN_004e3200`, none traced this pass), (b) inside the client-side prediction/render-interpolation path (`FUN_004c0bb0`, the likely `CL_Frame`, also not traced past its top level this pass), or (c) not a discrete accumulator at all but an emergent property of how movement/physics integration consumes the reported frametime (i.e. genuinely spread across many call sites, the "broadly hardcoded" outcome the plan's go/no-go question was written to detect). No evidence yet either confirms or rules out that broader-hardcoding possibility -- a systematic search for a hardcoded ~33ms/0.0333f constant used independently of `fixedtime`'s own value was NOT performed this pass (out of scope for the time available; a blunt float-bit-pattern scan across the whole binary would be the right next tool, not yet run).

**Recommendation (explicit, per the plan's own request)**: **not yet a clean go** -- and not yet a confirmed no-go either. What IS now confirmed: `fixedtime` is a real, working, correctly-understood lever that changes the elapsed-time VALUE reported once per (uncapped-cadence) `Com_Frame` call, in milliseconds. What remains unknown is whether simply setting it smaller (e.g. ~16-17ms) would actually make simulation logic execute more often/in smaller true steps, or whether some other, still-unfound mechanism inside `SV_Frame`/`CL_Frame`/movement-physics code independently locks real simulation work to a coarser cadence regardless of the reported delta -- which is precisely the scenario that would make this a broad, not small, undertaking. **Do not attempt a live `fixedtime` test based on findings to date** -- the risk is a "changed a client-reported delta but no observable behavior change" result that would be genuinely ambiguous to interpret without first finding the real per-tick consumer. Next real step: decompile `FUN_004c0bb0` (candidate `CL_Frame`) and `FUN_00424a50`'s remaining un-traced callees for a genuine msec/tick accumulator, or run a whole-binary scan for a hardcoded ~33ms float constant independent of `fixedtime`.
