## 92. Renderer-backend investigation (D3D11/12/Vulkan) -- DXVK parked as a real, un-evaluated VAC risk; D3D9On12 diagnostic added, awaiting one live launch (2026-08-26)

**Status:** Investigating -- research complete for both paths, diagnostic implemented and built clean, not yet live-confirmed.

**Context:** user asked about a D3D11/D3D12 renderer for this project (translating the game's real D3D9 calls directly) and Vulkan support, citing DXVK as precedent. Both investigated; they resolve very differently.

**DXVK (Vulkan) -- parked, not part of the active visual-suite plan.** Real, mature, MIT-licensed, genuinely usable as a native-Windows drop-in `d3d9.dll` replacement -- this project's own proxy DLL could in principle forward to DXVK's `d3d9.dll` instead of the real system one (same proxy-chaining technique already in use, just retargeted), and COM vtable layout for `IDirect3D9`/`IDirect3DDevice9` is a fixed interface contract, so this project's existing vtable-index hooks (`EndScene`=42, `Reset`=16, `CreateTexture`=23, `SetViewport`=47, etc.) would very likely keep working unmodified underneath it. **But**: multiple independent sources document that anti-cheat systems commonly treat DXVK's render-backend substitution as "tampering" -- a materially different, more systemic class of change than this project's existing input-remapping/shader-pass technique, and this specific combination (DXVK + MW3's own confirmed-active VAC, issue #33) has never been evaluated. Decision: parked here as a real roadmap idea, not pursued further without a dedicated, issue-#33-style VAC research pass first.

**D3D9On12 -- likely already active for free, diagnostic added to confirm.** A genuine Microsoft OS component, not a third-party DLL -- critically, it does NOT replace `d3d9.dll` at all. The app still creates its device through the real, genuine Microsoft `d3d9.dll` (the exact same one this project's proxy already forwards to); D3D9On12 sits one level below, as the actual driver-interface (DDI) implementation `d3d9.dll` talks to, entirely transparent to the calling app. Since nothing about the real `d3d9.dll` or its vtables changes, this sidesteps the DXVK anti-cheat concern entirely -- from the game's (and any anti-cheat's) perspective, it's still genuinely the real, unmodified system D3D9 API surface. Native D3D9 drivers are increasingly rare on modern GPU drivers, so this game may already be running through D3D9On12 today with zero code changes needed. Does **not** provide Vulkan support (Windows/D3D12 only).

**User note, addressed**: MSI Afterburner's overlay reports "D3D9_" for this game regardless of which backend is really active underneath -- Afterburner detects the API surface the app calls (still genuinely D3D9 either way, by design of D3D9On12's own transparency), not the real driver backend behind it. Expected, not evidence either way.

**Diagnostic implemented** (`proxy_d3d9/src/d3d9_hook.cpp`, `Hook_CreateDevice`, right after the existing `[res-diag]` block): two independent, real checks, logged as raw evidence rather than a guessed conclusion --
1. `GetModuleHandleA("d3d9on12.dll")` -- Microsoft's own documentation confirms this DLL loads into the process specifically when a D3D9On12 device is created, so a non-null handle is a direct positive.
2. `IDirect3D9::GetAdapterIdentifier` (vtable index 5, same fixed-layout class of call this project already relies on for `GetAdapterModeCount`/`EnumAdapterModes` at indices 6/7) -- D3D9On12 is documented to report itself distinctly in `Driver`/`Description` versus a real GPU vendor driver filename (e.g. `nvldumdx.dll`/`aticfx64.dll`).

Logs as `[d3d9on12-diag] d3d9on12.dll loaded=<yes/no> adapter driver="..." description="..."`. No config gate (harmless, automatic, one-shot per `CreateDevice` call, same class as this project's other narrow one-shot diagnostics). **Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors), `d3d9.dll` redeployed.**

**RESULT, confirmed live (2026-08-26)**: `[d3d9on12-diag] d3d9on12.dll loaded=no adapter driver="nvldumd.dll" description="NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti"` -- this system runs the game through a real, direct native NVIDIA D3D9 driver, NOT D3D9On12. **Status: RESOLVED (research question answered, real negative result).** This means the "D3D11/12 backward compat may already be active for free" hope does NOT hold on this system -- it's already on the fastest, most direct native D3D9 path, which is the best case for raw performance but means an actual D3D11/12 renderer (if ever pursued) would be genuine new work, not something already transparently happening. Does not change DXVK's own parked status above (that path still requires the real, un-evaluated VAC risk research before any further action).

### Follow-up, same day: [Video] ForceD3D9On12 flag implemented, per direct user request ("lets do a force D3D9on12 flag")

Since this system isn't using D3D9On12 by default, the user asked for a way to force it on directly, to test whether it helps or hurts on real hardware. Real mechanism, confirmed via Microsoft's own DirectX-Specs documentation before implementing (not guessed):

- The real system `d3d9.dll` exports `Direct3DCreate9On12` as a genuine, documented alternate entry point (`IDirect3D9* WINAPI Direct3DCreate9On12(UINT SDKVersion, D3D9ON12_ARGS* pOverrideList, UINT NumOverrideEntries)`) -- calling it is NOT a third-party renderer swap, it's the same real DLL this proxy already forwards to, just a different real export. `NumOverrideEntries=0` behaves identically to the ordinary `Direct3DCreate9` per Microsoft's own docs, so a real override entry (`Enable9On12=TRUE`, `pD3D12Device`/`ppD3D12Queues` left null so D3D9On12 creates its own internally) is required to actually force it on.
- `D3D_SDK_VERSION` = 32 (0x20) -- the same real value this project's own earlier RE already confirmed the game itself passes to the ordinary `Direct3DCreate9` (`FUN_0067a320`'s decompile).
- Implemented in `proxy_d3d9/src/dllmain.cpp`: the proxy's own `Direct3DCreate9` export (already implemented directly, not forwarded, so it can hook the returned interface) now checks `[Video] ForceD3D9On12` and, if enabled, calls the real `Direct3DCreate9On12` instead -- with a null-safe fallback to the ordinary path if the real export is missing or returns null. Either path returns a real `IDirect3D9*` with the same standard vtable layout, so `HookD3D9CreateDevice`/every downstream hook is completely unaffected by which path was taken.
- New config key `[Video] ForceD3D9On12` (`mod_config.h`/`.cpp`, schema v22->v23), default `0`/off.
- Also fixed a stale doc comment caught in the same pass: `InternalRenderScalePercent`'s `WriteDefaultConfig` ini-comment text still described the abandoned `r_mode`/`vid_restart` mechanism (correct everywhere else in the codebase after issue #88's final correction, just missed here) -- corrected to describe the real, shipped mechanism and cite the live 220fps/70-80fps confirmation.

**Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors), `d3d9.dll` redeployed. NOT YET LIVE-TESTED** -- next step: enable the flag, launch, and check `[d3d9on12-diag]`'s own output (already wired from the section above) to confirm `d3d9on12.dll loaded=yes` and the adapter `Driver`/`Description` fields now report D3D9On12 instead of the real native driver, then assess whether performance/stability actually improves or regresses on this hardware.

### First live test (2026-08-26): confirmed force worked, but crashed ("DX unrecoverable error") ~3 seconds into Survival with InternalRenderScalePercent=300 also active

Log confirms both the force AND the render-scale override genuinely applied: `[d3d9on12-force] ForceD3D9On12 enabled -- calling real Direct3DCreate9On12 instead of Direct3DCreate9`, `[d3d9on12-diag] d3d9on12.dll loaded=yes adapter driver="nvldumd.dll" description="NVIDIA GeForce RTX 2080 Ti"` (D3D9On12 genuinely active), `[video-scale] InternalRenderScalePercent=300 -> native=2560x1440 target=7680x4320` (the 9x-pixel-count override also genuinely applied). Game crashed with a real "DX unrecoverable error" a few seconds into Survival.

**Real, plausible explanation, not yet confirmed**: this system already confirmed 300% render scale is stable on the REAL native driver alone (220fps/70-80fps, no crash, earlier this session). Stacking that same 9x-pixel-count load (across ~9 separate deferred-rendering render targets -- `RESOLVED_SCENE`/`FLOAT_Z`/`SSAO`/`SSAO_BLURRED`/`SSAO_FLOAT_Z`/`POST_EFFECT_0`/`1`/`PINGPONG_0`/`1`, per issue #88's own `FUN_00683060` decompile) on top of D3D9On12's own real, heavier D3D12-translation overhead is a genuinely large combined VRAM/compute demand -- consistent with a real DXGI/TDR-style device-removed error, not necessarily a bug in either feature's own implementation.

**Isolating now**: `InternalRenderScalePercent` dropped back to 100 (normal load) while `ForceD3D9On12` stays enabled, to test D3D9On12 alone under ordinary conditions before concluding anything about either feature individually. Result pending.

### Isolation result (2026-08-26): D3D9On12 alone (InternalRenderScalePercent=100) is STABLE, and direct user report -- "the game with this flag force genuinely looks 10x better"

Confirms the crash was the STACKED combination (D3D9On12 + 300% render scale), not D3D9On12 itself being broken -- D3D9On12 alone, at normal (100%) render scale, ran without the "DX unrecoverable error" seen before.

**Real, unexpected, and significant finding**: the user reports a genuine, noticeable visual quality improvement with `ForceD3D9On12=1` even at 1x scale -- not just "no crash," an actual perceived quality upgrade. D3D9On12 is *supposed* to be a faithful DDI-level translation (same D3D9 semantics, different backend), not a quality change -- this is real, live-reported evidence that isn't yet explained by anything already confirmed in this issue.

**Leading theory, direct user reasoning (2026-08-26): "the 2080 Ti came out long after DX9 was a serious consideration, DX11 was more than standard by then."** Genuinely credible, and consistent with the real, already-cited fact this issue's own earlier section already established -- native D3D9 drivers are increasingly rare/deprioritized on modern GPU driver stacks. An RTX 2080 Ti (2018) launched years after NVIDIA's real engineering investment had already shifted to D3D11/12 -- the native D3D9 driver code path (`nvldumd.dll`) on a card this modern is very plausibly a legacy, minimally-maintained path, while D3D9On12 rides on top of the actively-developed, actively-optimized D3D12 driver stack. This would directly explain a real quality difference (texture filtering/sampling precision, MSAA resolve behavior) without needing any exotic mechanism -- the D3D12 backend is simply the driver code NVIDIA still actually invests in. Not independently verified via a driver changelog/vendor statement, but the strongest, most plausible explanation found so far; treat as the leading theory, not yet fully confirmed.

**Status: Partially Resolved -- the crash is now understood (stacking, not D3D9On12 itself) and D3D9On12-alone is confirmed stable+visually improved, with a credible explanation for why.** Given the positive result, this flag is a real candidate to eventually graduate toward recommended-on (still opt-in for now, given only one system has tested it, and the earlier crash proves real limits exist under heavy combined load) -- not a decision made this pass.

### Threshold narrowing (2026-08-26): 225% ALSO crashes under D3D9On12 -- safe range is narrower than hoped, somewhere between 100% and 225%

`InternalRenderScalePercent=225` with `ForceD3D9On12=1` crashed too, same "DX unrecoverable error" class as the 300% test. Real log evidence right before the crash: `[frame-benchmark] SLOW FRAME #811: 274.09ms` (a real, severe frame-time spike -- roughly 10x this session's typical slow-frame values), immediately followed by `[inlevel-flag-diag] restart spike detected (val=200) -- gate window re-armed` and `[overlay-hud] Reset() called -- releasing this project's own cached textures first`, then the log simply ends (no further lines, consistent with the process being killed by a real unrecoverable device error before any more log output could be written/flushed). This is a real, second data point for the same explanation as the 300% crash -- a genuine GPU stall/device-lost event under combined D3D9On12 + elevated render-scale load, not a code-path-specific bug isolated to 300% only.

**Known range so far**: 100% confirmed stable; 225% and 300% both confirmed crash. The real safe ceiling for `InternalRenderScalePercent` under `ForceD3D9On12` on this specific hardware is somewhere between 100% and 225%, not yet narrowed further.

**Separate, minor finding, same test session**: a real but slight visual artifact observed on the main menu specifically, appearing consistently ~5 seconds after launch, then never recurring for the rest of the session. Not yet investigated -- plausibly D3D9On12's own translation-layer warm-up (building its internal D3D12-side shader/pipeline caches on first use, a known general characteristic of translation layers, though not confirmed specifically documented for D3D9On12) rather than a lasting correctness bug, given it self-resolved and didn't recur. Logged here so it isn't lost; not currently blocking, no dedicated investigation done.

### `ResourceUsageLogging` diagnostic added, and a second real incident: a `vid_restart` (fullscreen<->borderless toggle) under `ForceD3D9On12` corrupted NVIDIA's own persistent D3D12 pipeline cache -- fixed with a real preventive guard

Added `[Experimental] ResourceUsageLogging` (`dllmain.cpp`'s new `ResourceLogThreadProc`, its own dedicated background thread per this project's established architecture) to check whether the 225%/300% crashes were real address-space/memory exhaustion. iw5sp.exe's PE header was checked directly first and DOES have `IMAGE_FILE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE` set (`Characteristics=0x0123`), ruling out the "capped at 2GB" version of that theory -- the diagnostic logs real `K32GetProcessMemoryInfo`/`GlobalMemoryStatusEx` data once a second to check the broader "still hits the real ~4GB 32-bit ceiling" version directly.

**Real capture, 225%+`ForceD3D9On12`**: memory stayed flat and healthy the entire session (~670MB working set, ~2.3GB available virtual address space, both stable for the whole log, no climb toward any ceiling) -- this specific failure was NOT memory/address-space exhaustion. Also surfaced a real, secondary observation: `Direct3DCreate9` is called TWICE at startup (the game likely does an adapter-capability probe then a real creation), each hitting `[d3d9on12-force]`'s real-`Direct3DCreate9On12`-forwarding path -- investigated as a possible cause (a stale trampoline if the two calls hooked different real `CreateDevice` addresses) but REFUTED by direct log evidence: both `MH_CreateHook(CreateDevice @ ...)` calls target the exact same address (`704E0060`), with the second correctly returning `MH_ERROR_ALREADY_CREATED` (status 3) -- a harmless, expected no-op, not a bug.

**Real incident, direct user account**: separately, switching display mode (fullscreen -> borderless, via the vanilla native Options menu, which triggers a real `vid_restart` -- already known broken under this project's hooks per issue #91) while `ForceD3D9On12` was active left the game rendering NOTHING (menu logic/input kept working) on every subsequent launch -- persistent across a full game restart, and NOT explained by a corrupted saved value (`players2/config.cfg`'s own `r_mode`/`r_displayMode` were checked directly and were valid, real, non-corrupt settings). **Root cause, confirmed by fix**: NVIDIA's own persistent D3D12 pipeline-state cache (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\DXCache`, found to be 12.9GB / 325 files, shared across every D3D game on the system, not MW3-specific) had a corrupted/incomplete entry from the broken `vid_restart` event, which kept getting reused on every subsequent launch regardless of this project's own config or the game's own saved settings. Manually clearing the cache and relaunching fixed it immediately, confirming the theory.

**This was a recovery, not a fix -- the real trigger (issue #91's `vid_restart` instability) was still live and could recur.** Direct user framing: "we must fix it... preventative, as d3d12 tl is better graphically and will possibly become the default if solid" -- correct call, given the real, live-confirmed visual improvement `ForceD3D9On12` already produced this session. **Real preventive fix implemented**: `Hook_CbufAddText` (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`), a new hook on the real `Cbuf_AddText`-equivalent (`0x00457c90`, already known via `real_settings.cpp`'s own `CbufAddText` binding) -- this is the SAME real function the vanilla native menu's own internal `.menu`-script `exec` actions use to queue console commands, so hooking it (not just this project's own `QueueConsoleCommand` wrapper, which the native menu never calls) is what actually lets this project see and block a native-menu-triggered `vid_restart`, not only ones this project's own code might queue. While `[Video] ForceD3D9On12` is enabled, any queued command containing `vid_restart` (case-insensitive) is dropped entirely before it reaches the real trampoline -- the player instead sees a real, visible warning via `ShowOverlayMessage` explaining why, rather than the input being silently eaten. Every other command passes through completely unmodified. Installed alongside this project's other engine-address hooks (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`'s main hook-install block).

**Refined same pass, two direct user corrections**: (1) the guard originally only checked `ForceD3D9On12` -- broadened to also cover `InternalRenderScalePercent > 0`, since that feature's own render targets are likewise only ever sized once at real startup (issue #88's "applied exactly ONCE per process" finding), and a live `vid_restart` tearing the device down mid-session is equally unverified territory for it, not just for `ForceD3D9On12`. (2) The original warning used a normal, auto-expiring `ShowOverlayMessage` toast (6s) -- direct instruction: "we should lock down vid restart and make our own popup that has to be dismissed." Added `ShowOverlayMessageUntilDismissed` (`overlay_hud.cpp`/`.h`, a new `g_overlayRequiresDismiss` mode on the existing overlay-message system) -- stays on screen indefinitely until the player presses Enter/Space/left-click (a 200ms guard prevents the same click that triggered the block from also instantly dismissing it), rather than a toast that could fade before being read. Also corrected the message text itself (a further direct correction: "the user shouldnt have to disable it, we should just block the vid restart calls") -- the popup no longer instructs the player to edit `mw3ncp_config.ini`, since the command is already unconditionally blocked regardless of what they do; it now just states a restart is required and why.

**Third correction, same pass, a real miss caught live**: the first implementation's dismiss check only covered keyboard (Enter/Space) and mouse (`IsLeftMouseButtonHeld()`) -- completely missing controller input, direct and pointed: "why enter space/click.. its a CONTROLLER PROJECT." Fixed via `Controller_GetRawButtonsAndTriggers` (`controller_input.h`, already used throughout `analog_input_hooks.cpp` for exactly this class of raw-button read) checking the real `XINPUT_GAMEPAD_A` bit (`0x1000`), matching this project's own established "A = confirm" convention used elsewhere (pause menu, glyph editor).

**Fourth correction, same pass -- real visual rework, direct spec: "glyph too and the ui should look styled like our menu as a small 200-250px(@1080p) warning popup modal."** The original warning used the SAME shared toast texture every other overlay notification uses (`g_textTexture`) -- discovered mid-implementation that this canvas is hardcoded to 512x64 with `DT_SINGLELINE` throughout `RenderMaskLuminance`/`RenderTextToArgbBuffer` (fixed-size static buffers, no word-wrap), genuinely unsuited to a multi-line paragraph without real risk to that already-proven, heavily-used pipeline. Built a real, separate system instead:
- New `kWarningTextureWidth`/`kWarningTextureHeight` canvas (640x160), its own `g_warningTextTexture`, and a real word-wrapped (`DT_WORDBREAK | DT_CENTER`, not `DT_SINGLELINE`) text-mask renderer (`RenderWarningTextMask`/`RenderWarningTextToArgbBuffer`/`EnsureWarningTextTexture`) -- same two-pass outline+fill compositing technique as the existing pipeline, deliberately not sharing its buffers.
- `DrawWarningModal` (`overlay_hud.cpp`, defined after `DrawBlurredBackgroundRegion` so its dependencies -- `GetResolutionScale`, `DrawBlurredBackgroundRegion`, `GetOrLoadGlyphIconTexture`, `DrawGenericTexturedQuad` -- are all already defined) composes the real modal: a 640x225 (@1080p design space, satisfying the "200-250px" spec) blurred panel via `DrawBlurredBackgroundRegion` (reusing the exact same blur-capture mechanism the custom Options screen already uses -- genuinely "styled like our menu," not a new visual language), the wrapped explanation text centered in the upper portion, and the real controller A-glyph (`GetControllerGlyphAssetName`/`GetOrLoadGlyphIconTexture`, this project's own established glyph-resolution system, same three-call pattern already used for the Options screen's own row-confirm A-glyph) drawn near the bottom as a decorative accent -- not pixel-locked inline with a specific word in the text (real per-glyph text-layout measurement judged out of scope for this warning).
- `DrawOverlayMessage` now branches to `DrawWarningModal` instead of the shared toast draw path whenever `g_overlayRequiresDismiss` is set; the shared toast pipeline itself is completely untouched.
- `g_warningTextTexture` added to both existing device-recreation cleanup call sites (`releaseIfSet(g_textTexture)`'s own two real call sites), matching the existing precedent for `g_textTexture` -- avoids a stale/dangling texture pointer surviving a real device recreation (issue #91-adjacent territory).
- Popup text shortened accordingly ("Enter / Space / Click, or:") since the real glyph icon now visually covers the controller case rather than needing to be spelled out in words too.

**Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors), `d3d9.dll` redeployed. NOT YET LIVE-TESTED** -- next step: with `ForceD3D9On12=1` (or `InternalRenderScalePercent > 0`), attempt a real display-mode change (fullscreen<->borderless, or a Resolution change) via the vanilla native Options menu and confirm the dismiss-required warning appears and stays up until acknowledged, the game does NOT go dark/corrupt, and normal, non-video settings changes are completely unaffected.

### Live-tested (2026-08-26): the guard did NOT resolve the underlying black screen -- deep RE investigation into forcing a real device teardown+recreate, then a decisive external finding that redirects the whole feature's status

Live retest with the guard installed still black-screened under `ForceD3D9On12=1` + `InternalRenderScalePercent=225`, with NO display-mode change involved this time -- the log showed the exact same `SWF_COMMON_DESC_RESIZE_POPUP_NAME` cycling signature as the earlier borderless incident. **Direct user correction: that popup is normal/expected on any video Apply and is not itself the bug** -- the real issue is that the device (and D3D9On12's own internal D3D12 backend) persists when it should be destroyed and recreated.

**Real RE trail, confirming the mechanism precisely:**
- `DAT_021cd924` (the engine's cached `IDirect3D9*`) has exactly two real writers: `FUN_0067a320` (only writes if currently null -- i.e., only ever fires once, at genuine startup) and `FUN_0067a690`, a real, complete teardown function that genuinely `Release()`s both the device (`DAT_021cd928`) and the interface itself (`DAT_021cd924`), nulling both.
- `FUN_0067a690` has exactly ONE real caller, and that caller's own call chain ends in `_exit(0)` -- **the real, full device+interface teardown only ever happens at genuine process exit, never during a live in-session display-mode change.** Live display-mode-change events instead go through `FUN_00427490`'s lighter path (`FUN_00433eb0(0)`, param 0 deliberately skips calling `FUN_0067a690`), which never releases the device or interface.
- Traced the device-lost-check chain (`FUN_0067a4a0`/`FUN_0067a320`, reached via `FUN_004251b0`'s own flag-gated dispatch) up through `FUN_0044c7b0`, confirmed as the real per-frame `Com_Frame` wrapper (calls the real `FUN_00458600` immediately after a `"Com_Frame_Try_Block_Function"` profiler-string marker) -- this chain IS reachable from real, recurring in-session events (disconnect/level-exit/return-to-menu), not just startup, though not on a true continuous per-frame basis.
- **Real, concrete fix design reached** (not yet implemented): from `Hook_CbufAddText`, on a detected `vid_restart`, call `FUN_0067a690()` (real teardown) then `FUN_0067a320()` (real recreate, which -- with both globals now null -- falls through to a genuine fresh `Direct3DCreate9` call, re-triggering our own `ForceD3D9On12` force) synchronously, ourselves, rather than blocking the command or waiting for a natural session-transition event.
- **Real, named risk that stopped this from being implemented blind**: this runs synchronously inside `Cbuf_AddText`'s own call context. If the calling menu code cached a raw pointer to the OLD device before calling `Cbuf_AddText` and touches it again after our hook returns (same frame), that's a real use-after-free -- best case an instant crash, worst case silent heap corruption surfacing later. A second, unruled-out risk: other engine subsystems (audio/UI/renderer) could hold their own separate cached copies of the device pointer we haven't traced, which wouldn't get updated by this fix. A third, softer risk: `FUN_0067a320`'s own creation sequence was written assuming startup/session-transition timing, not synchronous mid-frame re-entry from a menu-input callback.

**Root-cause investigation, ruling out the "persists across a fresh process launch" mystery one candidate at a time, all with real evidence, not guesses:**
- Checked `iw5sp.exe`'s own PE header directly: `IMAGE_FILE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE` IS set -- rules out the specific "32-bit process capped at 2GB" theory (a real, un-guessed check).
- Added `[Experimental] ResourceUsageLogging` (`dllmain.cpp`'s `ResourceLogThreadProc`, real `K32GetProcessMemoryInfo`/`GlobalMemoryStatusEx` data once a second) -- real capture at 225%+`ForceD3D9On12` showed memory flat and healthy the entire session (~670MB working set, ~2.3GB available virtual address space, never climbing toward any ceiling). **Not memory/address-space exhaustion.**
- Checked the real Windows System event log for genuine GPU/display-driver TDR (Timeout Detection and Recovery) events in the hours around the failures: **zero found.** This rules out a genuine hardware-level GPU hang/driver crash -- whatever "DX unrecoverable error" the user saw was the game's own application-level response to a real D3D device-lost condition, not a driver-level reset Windows had to log and recover from.
- Checked the real, live current Windows desktop/display state directly (`System.Windows.Forms.Screen`, WMI `Win32_VideoController`): normal, primary monitor correctly reporting its real native resolution, no evidence of a stuck/wrong display mode at the OS level.
- Checked `players2/config.cfg`'s own saved `r_mode`/`r_displayMode` values directly: valid, not corrupted.
- **User directly tested and ruled out BOTH real candidate shader/pipeline caches** by deleting `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NVIDIA\DXCache` AND `%LOCALAPPDATA%\D3DSCache` (the generic, non-NVIDIA-specific Windows D3D shader cache) and confirming the black screen still recurs regardless. **Not a persistent cache artifact of any kind.** (This also retroactively confirms the earlier "DXCache clear fixed it" conclusion from earlier this same day was very likely a misattribution -- most plausibly coincidental timing, not a real causal fix, exactly as the user suspected when they caught this: "turns out the dx cache wasnt a fix at all.")
- Also directly confirmed via live log: the black screen recurs with `InternalRenderScalePercent` at normal/default scale too -- **this is genuinely `ForceD3D9On12`-specific, not tied to the render-scale feature at all**, despite earlier sessions treating them as a combined/stacked risk.

**Decisive external finding, redirects this feature's real status**: web research surfaced a real, open issue on Microsoft's own `microsoft/D3D9On12` GitHub repo -- ["d3d9on12 black screen" (issue #83)](https://github.com/microsoft/D3D9On12/issues/83) -- genuine, independently-reported black-screen bugs across multiple unrelated games and GPU vendors (including Intel UHD Graphics), with the wider community describing D3D9On12 as "still a raw product" with "serious problems." Separately, and structurally: **Direct3D 12 does not support true full-screen exclusive mode at all** -- it substitutes "full-screen optimizations" (FSO), a genuinely different mechanism from the real D3D9 exclusive-fullscreen semantics this 2011 engine's own fullscreen/display-mode code was written against. This is a real, credible, externally-documented explanation that doesn't require any bug in this project's own hooks at all -- D3D9On12 has known, real, widely-reported instability with exactly this symptom class, independent of any code this project has written.

**Status: Open, redirected -- NOT chasing the device-teardown-and-recreate fix further for now.** Given (a) the real, substantial risk profile of the only concrete fix design found (synchronous engine-internal device manipulation, multiple unruled-out failure modes), (b) the now-decisive external evidence that this is a known, real, unresolved class of bug in D3D9On12 itself, independent of this project, and (c) the sheer number of genuine, independent investigative rounds already spent on this today (crash reproduction, memory diagnostics, render-target RE, device-lifecycle RE, cache theory -- twice, TDR event log, display state) -- **`ForceD3D9On12` is being left OFF by default (already the case) and should be treated as genuinely unstable on at least this hardware/driver/engine combination, not a bug this project is expected to fix.** The real, confirmed positive result from earlier (a genuine, live-confirmed visual quality improvement at 100% scale) remains true and worth keeping the feature around for -- but it should ship labeled honestly as unstable/experimental, with this real investigation trail as the citation, rather than implied to be reliably safe.

### Two more isolation forks (2026-08-26), decisively clearing this project's own code, then final decision: no custom translation layer, chase the real visual improvement via native driver instead

Two parallel forks dispatched at the user's request ("lets do some forks into this"): (1) web research turned up a real, documented Windows Update regression (`KB5012643`, `d3d9on12.dll` faulting with exception `0xc0000094` on certain GPUs, fixed via later KBs) and multiple independent reports tying D3D9On12 crashes to Xbox Game Bar -- both real, standing system-level state that a GPU driver reset would never clear, a plausible fit for "survives Win+Ctrl+Shift+B." Directly checked: `GameBarPresenceWriter` confirmed actively running on this system, and the OS is on a genuinely bleeding-edge Windows 11 build (26200). (2) RE pass found `FUN_00682e50` (part of the render-target-allocation chain) conditionally creates a real multisampled render target when AA is enabled, and this install's own saved config has `r_aaSamples=4` -- MSAA is a well-precedented fragile area in D3D9-on-D3D12 translation layers generally.

**Before testing either lead, one more direct isolation request from the user** ("is it our overlay d3d9 holding the device?") -- checked this project's own code directly rather than guessing:
- Temporarily bypassed `Hook_EndScene` entirely (skip every one of this project's own draw calls -- Options menu, overlay toasts/warning modal, glyph icons, gameplay hints, cursor -- call straight through to the real `EndScene` unmodified) whenever `ForceD3D9On12` is active. **Still black-screened with zero overlay code running.** Rules out this project's own D3D9 resource caching/state changes as the cause.
- Read `Hook_CreateTexture` (`asset_capture.cpp`) directly: confirmed a genuine passthrough -- the real call happens first, completely unmodified, its result is always what's returned; the only unconditional added work is `QueryPerformanceCounter` timing (no LockRect/file I/O unless mid-capture, which is a separate, off-by-default gate).
- Read `Hook_Reset` directly: also a clean, standard pattern (release own caches, call real `Reset`, log its real `HRESULT`) -- but checking the actual log showed **`Reset()` never fires at all** this session (matches the earlier RE finding that this engine never calls it on a display change), and the real `CreateDevice` call itself succeeded cleanly (`hr=0x00000000`).

**With every one of this project's own hooks now cleared** (overlay drawing fully bypassed, `CreateTexture` confirmed passthrough, `Reset` confirmed never firing, device creation itself succeeding) and the device staying genuinely alive (menu logic/input keeps working, `EndScene` fires regularly) with nothing visibly rendering and zero error surfacing anywhere in this project's own logs -- this is about as close to "the device is valid but D3D9On12 itself never presents anything" as static investigation can get without a live debugger attach.

**Final decision (2026-08-26)**: the user initially proposed building a custom, from-scratch D3D9 translation layer capable of targeting multiple modern backends -- explicitly assessed as out of scope (the same class of undertaking as DXVK or D3D9On12 itself, multi-year efforts by dedicated teams; Microsoft's own D3D9On12, built by Microsoft's graphics engineers, is *still* the "raw product" this whole investigation is about) and not pursued. **The real underlying motivation was image sharpness, not D3D9On12 specifically** ("my issue is that it just looked so much sharper there") -- redirected to a much safer, already-proven-stable lever: this install's saved `r_texFilterAnisoMax`/`r_texFilterAnisoMin` were capped at 4/1 -- raised to 16/16 (`players2/config.cfg`, a real, already-understood, native-driver-only dvar, zero D3D9On12 involvement, effectively free on this hardware) as a live test for whether anisotropic filtering explains the perceived sharpness difference, rather than continuing to chase D3D9On12 itself.

**Cleanup, same pass**: both temporary diagnostics from this investigation removed -- the `Hook_CbufAddText` vid_restart guard (temporarily disabled for the earlier confound-isolation test, confirmed NOT the cause) re-enabled, since it's still real, needed protection against issue #91's vid_restart instability; the `Hook_EndScene` overlay-bypass diagnostic removed entirely now that its answer is captured. `[Video] ForceD3D9On12`'s own doc comment (`mod_config.h`, `mod_config.cpp`'s `WriteDefaultConfig` template, and the live deployed `mw3ncp_config.ini`) all updated to a direct "DO NOT USE -- CONFIRMED UNSTABLE" warning citing this full trail, per explicit user instruction ("explicitly note in the config that it shouldnt be used"). Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors) after each change, `d3d9.dll` redeployed.

**This closes out the `ForceD3D9On12` investigation for this session.** Real, useful, permanent outcomes even though the original feature isn't usable: (1) the `Cbuf_AddText` vid_restart guard is real, working, standalone protection against issue #91 regardless of `ForceD3D9On12`'s own status; (2) the `[Experimental] ResourceUsageLogging` diagnostic is real, reusable infrastructure for any future memory-related investigation; (3) the D3D9On12-active diagnostic (`[d3d9on12-diag]`) stays in place, harmless and informative, confirming which backend is really in use on any given system.

## 93. Phase A (visual-suite plan) full-screen passthrough crashed on init -- this specific init-crash bug RESOLVED, but Phase A overall NOT done, blocked on issue #96's still-open crash regression (2026-08-26)

**Status:** The init-crash bug this entry originally tracked (a real
type-confusion bug on a `Release()` call) is resolved and confirmed live
("yep no crash this time") -- launches clean with `FullScreenPassthroughTest=1`
active. **But direct user correction (2026-08-26, same standard already
applied to Phase E/issue #95): "A aswell isnt done either."** Phase A is the
foundation every later phase (B/E, eventually C/D/F) is built on, and a live,
reproducible crash regression (issue #96, root cause still unconfirmed) sits
in the exact same build this phase's pipeline lives in -- so Phase A stays
open/not-done alongside Phase E until #96 actually has a confirmed fix, not
just this entry's own narrower init-crash fix.

Live-reported immediately after deploying Phase A of the visual-suite plan
(`C:\Users\kyesa\.claude\plans\twinkly-tickling-gem.md`) with
`[Experimental] FullScreenPassthroughTest=1`: **"game crashes on init."**

**Round 1 (wrong theory, corrected in Round 2)**: initial Windows Event Log
check (`Get-WinEvent -FilterHashtable @{LogName='Application'; Id=1000}`) showed
an access violation (`0xc0000005`) INSIDE the real system
`C:\WINDOWS\system32\d3d9.dll`, ruling out a dangling pointer as the direct
fault site and pointing at a bad parameter into a real D3D9 call. Guessed the
cause was an MSAA-resolve `StretchRect` requiring `Filter=D3DTEXF_NONE` (the
live config has `r_aaSamples="4"`) -- fixed the filter parameter, rebuilt,
redeployed. **User re-tested: "still crashes on launch immediately," with the
EXACT SAME fault offset (`0x0006274a`) in the same real `d3d9.dll` build even
after the fix** -- proof the filter theory was wrong; an identical fault site
across a code change that should have altered the call means the real cause
was still unidentified.

**Round 2 (real root cause, confirmed via bracketed diagnostic logging)**:
rather than guess a third time, added a temporary `[fsp-diag]` log line before
and after every real D3D9 call in `DrawFullScreenPass`/
`RunFullScreenPostProcessIfEnabled`, gated to the first 3 calls only (avoids
reproducing the "22GB log" issue this project already fixed once, since this
function runs every frame). This project's existing `FlushLogOnCrash`
(`dllmain.cpp`, an `AddVectoredExceptionHandler` that flushes the log and
always returns `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH`) guarantees every line logged before
a real crash reaches disk. The very next launch pinpointed the fault exactly:
the log reached `"step 7: StretchRect returned (survived)"` but never reached
`"step 8: surfaces released"` -- the crash is inside the two `Release()` calls
immediately after `StretchRect`. The same diagnostic also disproved the Round 1
MSAA theory directly: `GetDesc` on the real backbuffer showed
`MultiSampleType=0` -- the backbuffer was never multisampled on this system at
all.

**Real root cause**: `captureSurface` (an `IDirect3DSurface9*`, obtained via
`GetSurfaceLevel` on `g_fullscreenCaptureTexture`) was being released through
`captureTexVtbl` -- the TEXTURE's own vtable, cached earlier in the function for
the `GetSurfaceLevel` call -- instead of the SURFACE's own vtable.
`IUnknown::Release` sits at the same vtable slot (2) on every D3D9 COM
interface, but the actual compiled function body differs per real implementing
class (a texture's `Release()` and a surface's `Release()` manage different
internal object layouts). Calling the TEXTURE's `Release()` implementation with
a SURFACE pointer as `this` is genuine type confusion -- the texture's
`Release()` code walked into memory laid out for a different class of object,
corrupting state and crashing deep inside the real `d3d9.dll`'s own
implementation. **This is the same bug CLASS `DrawBlurredBackgroundRegion`'s own
header comment already documents** (`GetSurfaceLevel` fetched via `deviceVtbl`
instead of the texture's own vtable, live-crashed once already, fixed
2026-08-05) -- a second, independent instance of "cached the wrong object's
vtable pointer and reused it for a different object," this time on `Release()`
instead of `GetSurfaceLevel`. `DrawBlurredBackgroundRegion` itself never had
this specific bug -- it already fetches each surface's own vtable fresh,
inline, at its own release call sites.

**Fix**: `DrawFullScreenPass` now fetches `captureSurface`'s own vtable
(`*reinterpret_cast<void***>(captureSurface)`) immediately before releasing it,
exactly matching `DrawBlurredBackgroundRegion`'s own established pattern.
`D3DTEXF_NONE` (the Round 1 change) was left in place -- still the technically
correct choice for a non-stretching 1:1 copy even though it wasn't the actual
crash cause, and reverting it back to `POINT` would have been a needless extra
variable to change while re-testing.

**Process lesson**: Round 1 guessed from a plausible-sounding D3D9 API rule
without direct evidence, and the identical fault offset after that "fix" was
the actual signal the guess was wrong -- worth noticing immediately rather than
assuming the fix just needed more testing. Round 2 used the crash-safe
diagnostic-logging technique already available in this codebase
(`FlushLogOnCrash`) to get a real, exact answer on the first attempt instead of
guessing again. This is 2 genuine rounds total, not the 5-6+ this project's own
principle 9 threshold requires before considering a bigger pivot (e.g. the
"scrap AA in favour of forking d3d9to12" idea floated mid-investigation) --
resolved well before that threshold, no pivot needed.

Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors) after each change, `d3d9.dll` redeployed
each time. Confirmed live the same session -- clean launch, no crash.

**Still outstanding**: this only confirms the pipeline no longer crashes, not
yet that the frame is visually IDENTICAL with the passthrough active (Phase A's
own real deliverable per the visual-suite plan, needed before Phase B/RCAS
builds a real effect on top of it) -- a separate visual confirmation from the
user.

## 94. Phase B (visual-suite plan): FSR 1.0 RCAS full-screen sharpening -- built, deployed, not yet live-tuned (2026-08-26)

**Status:** Built and deployed, not yet live-confirmed for visual quality.

First real effect on top of Phase A's capture/composite pipeline (issue #93):
FSR 1.0 RCAS (Robust Contrast Adaptive Sharpening), a direct port of AMD's real
FidelityFX-FSR reference source (`ffx_fsr1.h`, `FsrRcasF`/`FsrRcasCon`, MIT
license) -- fetched and verified line-for-line against the real GitHub source,
not reconstructed from memory. Full port-fidelity notes (what's a faithful
translation vs. a deliberate simplification of AMD's own UX scaffolding) live in
`re_notes/shaders/fsr_rcas.hlsl`'s own header comment.

**ps_2_0 doesn't fit**: tried first, matching this project's usual convention --
fxc reports 74 arithmetic instruction slots needed, ps_2_0's real hard cap is
64 (`error X5608`). RCAS's real per-pixel math (5-tap neighborhood, min/max
ring, noise detection, an exact contrast-clip solve) is bigger than the
existing 9-tap blur/passthrough shaders. Compiled as `ps_3_0` instead (71
slots, well within budget) -- safe on this project's real dev hardware (RTX
2080 Ti, native SM3+ for well over a decade). Per the plan's own text ("check
real device pixel-shader-version caps before committing to which"),
`EnsureRcasShader` (`overlay_hud.cpp`) checks the real device's
`PixelShaderVersion` cap via `GetDeviceCaps` before loading this shader, and
refuses gracefully (no sharpening, not a crash) on hardware below SM3.

**A new, minimal, byte-layout-verified `D3DCAPS9_MinimalLocal` struct** was
added for this check (avoids a full `d3d9.h` include, same convention as
`dllmain.cpp`'s `D3D9ON12_ARGS_LOCAL`) -- every field up to and including
`PixelShaderVersion` is declared by its real name/type, confirmed against a
direct fetch of the real `d3d9caps.h` field order (51 consecutive 4-byte
fields, no padding), with a deliberately oversized trailing pad buffer (512
bytes past `PixelShaderVersion`, real struct is ~300 bytes total) since the
real `GetDeviceCaps` call writes the COMPLETE struct regardless of how much of
it is declared -- undersizing this would be a real stack overflow, the exact
bug class issue #93 already found once this session (on `Release()`, not
`GetDeviceCaps`), applied preemptively here instead of found via a crash.

**Config**: `[Video] FsrSharpenEnabled` (default off) + `FsrSharpenStrength`
(0.0-1.0, default 0.5) -- passed straight through as RCAS's real `con.x`
sharpen-lobe scale, skipping AMD's stops/exp2 UX framing (not part of
`FsrRcasF`'s actual per-pixel math, just AMD's own parameter presentation
choice -- see the HLSL file's header comment). `DrawFullScreenPass` (Phase A)
was extended with an optional shader-constant-setup callback
(`FullScreenShaderSetupFn`) so each real effect can bind its own pixel shader
constants after `SetPixelShader` -- RCAS sets `c0`=texelSize, `c1.x`=sharpness;
a future FXAA/motion-blur pass would do the same. RCAS takes priority over
Phase A's own passthrough-test shader when both happen to be enabled (mutually
exclusive single-shader passes for now -- an ordered multi-pass list is future
work once more than one real effect exists, per the plan's own Phase A text).

Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors), `d3d9.dll` redeployed, `[Video]
FsrSharpenEnabled=1`/`FsrSharpenStrength=0.50` set live in
`mw3ncp_config.ini` for testing. Not yet live-confirmed -- next launch is the
real check, both for stability and for whether 0.5 strength looks right or
needs retuning.

**Live feedback, same day: "needs more softness."** `FsrSharpenStrength` lowered
0.5 -> 0.3 (both the compiled default in `mod_config.h` and the live config).

gets blurred on top rather than the reverse -- an explicit ordering choice

guessed or left at decompiler-inferred confidence)**:
1. Confirmed `R_RENDERTARGET_RESOLVED_SCENE` is a real, separate off-screen

   (things rendering INTO it), confirming the real composite doesn't read
   this specific global directly.
3. Pivoted following a direct user re-steer ("remember we located the ui res
   scale id look arund there... diff render res... would possibly be the
   coupling mech") -- reused this SAME session's own `InternalRenderScalePercent`

   `FUN_004e5b30` (a real viewport-RECT compute function) and found a genuine
   mode flag at `DAT_02802f60+0x1760`: mode==1 selects a FULL-SCREEN rect
   (0,0,w,h); anything else selects the 3D scene's own sub-rect
   (`+0x174c..58`, the exact field issue #88's own render-scale feature
   already reads/writes).
4. Found the real writer of that mode flag: `FUN_004f7b40`, which sets
   mode=1, does ONE 2D draw call, then RESTORES the previous mode --
   confirming this function wraps EVERY individual native 2D HUD/UI element
   draw, not a once-per-frame toggle. Its own calling convention (raw
   disassembly) turned out to be a genuinely risky mix of register- and
   stack-passed args -- NOT hooked directly; too much room to get wrong for
   a function called this often (every HUD/UI element, every frame).
5. Found its caller, `FUN_00697ce0` -- assigns a `POST_EFFECT` render target
   into a texture slot with real letterbox/aspect-ratio math around it, a
   strong composite-function signature -- and ITS single caller,
   `FUN_00497210`: the real per-viewport scene-finish orchestrator
   (composites the resolved scene, runs the engine's own real post-effects,
   draws a couple of specific overlay textures). **Confirmed via raw
   disassembly (not the decompiler's guessed signature) to be a plain,
   all-stack-args `__cdecl` function** -- no risky convention to get wrong,
   called once per active viewport (`FUN_00694650`'s own loop; once per frame
   for this project's real single-viewport scope, no splitscreen support).

**Real fix, implemented same session**: a new engine hook,
`Hook_FUN_00497210` (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`), a POST-hook on
`FUN_00497210` (address `0x00497210`) -- the real trampoline runs completely
unmodified first (both of its own real arguments forwarded byte-for-byte,
untouched, since this hook doesn't need to understand either one), THEN
`TriggerMotionBlurFromEngineHook()` (`overlay_hud.cpp`, new `extern "C"`
forwarder -- deliberately matching this file's own already-validated
anonymous-namespace-plus-`extern "C"` linkage pattern, header declaration
updated to match exactly) fires the motion-blur pass. This runs AFTER the
real scene composite but BEFORE the engine's own native HUD/UI drawing (which
happens later, via the `FUN_004f39e0`/`FUN_004f7b40` chain found in step 4 --
deliberately not hooked directly, per that step's own risk reasoning). The
motion-blur trigger was moved OUT of `Hook_EndScene`'s own top (Round 2's call
site) to this new, genuinely earlier hook point; this project's own overlay
(drawn inside `Hook_EndScene`, later still) remains excluded exactly as Round
2 already achieved -- this is a strictly earlier hook, not a replacement for
that ordering.

Built clean via MSBuild (0 errors, including no linker errors -- real
confirmation the new cross-file `extern "C"` linkage resolved correctly) and
redeployed. Not yet re-confirmed live by the user -- next launch is the real
check, both for stability (a new hardcoded hook target, `MH_CreateHook`'s own
return code is the install-time validation per this project's standard) and
for whether native HUD elements are now genuinely excluded from the blur.

**Round 4 (2026-08-26, real crash investigation, not guessed): per-frame
multi-fire guard.** Documentation-only entry, added retroactively during the
2026-08-26 parallel fork pass on issue #96 -- this fix was already live in
code (`g_motionBlurRanThisFrame`, `overlay_hud.cpp:3331-3363`, its own header
comment already labeled "ROUND 4 FIX") but had never actually been written up
under its own heading here, so issue #96 ended up citing "issue #95's own
Round 4 entry" for content that, until now, didn't exist at this heading --
a real doc-drift gap, now closed. The original comment above (Round 3) claimed
`FUN_00497210` runs "once per frame" -- WRONG, caught via this same live
crash investigation (memdiff livedump snapshots showed no memory-pressure
signature at all, redirecting the search toward this project's own newest
code instead of the native engine). `FUN_00497210`'s real caller is
`FUN_00508970`, a RECURSIVE rectangle-splitting function that carves the
viewport into sub-rectangles around exclusion zones (real splitscreen/
picture-in-picture support) and calls `FUN_00497210` SEPARATELY for each
resulting piece -- its base case (empty exclude list) calls it exactly once,
but any active exclusion (a PIP element, killcam, etc.) makes it fire
MULTIPLE TIMES in the same real frame. Each extra fire meant a second/third/
etc. full capture-and-redraw against a backbuffer still mid-composite between
sub-rectangle draws -- a real, intermittent (only when an exclusion zone is
actually active) state-corruption risk, not present every frame, which is
exactly why this never reproduced consistently. Fixed with a per-real-frame
guard (`g_motionBlurRanThisFrame`, reset once at the top of `Hook_EndScene`)
so this pass runs at most once per frame regardless of how many times the
engine hook itself fires. **Real and still correct, but confirmed (via issue
#96's own on/off/100% isolation test) NOT sufficient on its own to explain
the crash** -- the crash still reproduces tied to `InternalRenderScalePercent`
with this fix already in place. Left standing as a real, independent fix
regardless of how #96 resolves. `FUN_00508970`'s own exclusion-zone condition
is also, separately, a live candidate for driving issue #96's OWN mechanism
(see that issue's fork 1 findings) -- not confirmed to be the same trigger,
flagged as a next-RE-step there.

**Round 5 (2026-08-26, same day): real center-to-edge radial falloff.**
Direct user request: "motion blur shouls have a configurable middle to outer
blue setting ie less blurry in middle more blur on edges" -- a real, standard
technique (keeps the actual focal point sharp while peripheral vision smears
more, matching how motion blur is commonly implemented in racing/FPS titles).
`motion_blur.hlsl` now computes each pixel's UV-space distance from screen
center, normalized so a corner (the farthest on-screen point on any real
aspect ratio) maps to exactly 1.0, and scales the blur vector by
`lerp(1.0, dist, MotionBlurCenterFalloff)` -- at `MotionBlurCenterFalloff=0`
this collapses back to the original uniform blur; at `1.0` (the new default)
blur genuinely fades to ~0 at dead center. Recompiles clean as `ps_2_0` (36
instruction slots, still comfortably under the 64 cap -- no `ps_3_0` needed
for this addition). New `[Video] MotionBlurCenterFalloff` config value
(0.0-1.0, default 1.0). Built clean, redeployed, set live. Not yet
live-confirmed.

## 96. Game "literally exited" mid-session, no menu open -- isolated to `InternalRenderScalePercent` (issue #88); the SAVED_SCREEN-size "fix" was WRONG and has been reverted (2026-08-26)

**Status:** Open, but with 3 live, independent, unreconciled leads plus one
theory ruled out, as of a 2026-08-26 4-way parallel static-RE pass (see that
section, below the original investigation). Direct user isolation testing
narrowed the crash precisely to `InternalRenderScalePercent` being active at
any value (including 100%) -- solid, reproduced evidence. A theorized fix
(below) was built and DEPLOYED, then caught live by the user almost
immediately as actively harmful and has been reverted (clean rebuild, 0
errors, redeployed). The real root-cause mechanism is still unconfirmed --
next session's job is live-testing the 3 leads below, not more static
theorizing. Three earlier "found it" claims in this same investigation (VRAM
exhaustion; a Phase E multi-fire bug; the SAVED_SCREEN-size mismatch below)
have now all been disproved or retracted -- kept below for the record, not
deleted, since each was a real, good-faith, evidence-based attempt that
genuinely narrowed the search even while being wrong itself. **Demonware/
anti-tamper is ruled out** (see the parallel-pass section) -- this is a
controlled internal engine exit, not an external kill.

**Critical new live evidence (2026-08-26, direct user report, after the
parallel-pass section below was written): "its not vid_restart related IT
HAPPENS ONLY IN LIVE GAMEPLAY (Underground map crashes fastest)."** Two real
constraints this adds, neither satisfied by fork 4's `vid_restart`-guard
theory: (1) the crash ties to being IN GAMEPLAY specifically, not to menu/
settings actions that would plausibly issue a `vid_restart` (a video-options
change, an alt-tab recovery, etc.) -- there is no known live-gameplay action
that legitimately issues `vid_restart`, so that lead is now DEPRIORITIZED,
not actively disproved (the log check from fork 4 is still worth running if
convenient, but is no longer the top priority); (2) **crash SPEED is
MAP-DEPENDENT** ("Underground crashes fastest") -- a signature neither the
`vid_restart` guard nor a flat VRAM-exhaustion theory would produce on their
own (both would be roughly map-agnostic), but which fits BOTH remaining
leads well: fork 1's exclusion-zone/sub-rect viewport mismatch (if
`Underground` triggers that rendering path -- mirrors, security-camera/
turret-cam views, portal-heavy tunnel geometry -- more often or more
severely than other maps) and fork 2's unclamped shared depth-stencil (if
`Underground`'s geometry/lighting is simply more VRAM-demanding than other
maps, hitting a real driver-level rejection sooner). **This promotes forks 1
and 2 to top priority for next session, ahead of fork 4's log check** -- see
the re-ordered priority list at the end of the parallel-pass section. Open
question, not yet checked: does `Underground` have any in-game mirror/
camera/turret-cam/picture-in-picture rendering element? (Only checkable live
or via a map-asset GSC scan of `zone/english/mp_underground.ff`/
`so_survival_mp_underground.ff`, not yet attempted -- these are compressed
fastfiles, not plain text, so a real extraction step would be needed first.)
If confirmed, that would directly connect fork 1's exclusion-zone mechanism
to this specific map rather than leaving it a general theory.

**UPDATE, same day, direct user follow-up ("dig into it")**: traced the
mechanism all the way to real code -- see the "Deep RE dig" section below.
`FUN_00450740` computes a viewport sub-rect as an EXPLICIT ratio between
`DAT_021d2e00`/`04` (the pair this project's hook overrides) and
`DAT_021d2e08`/`0c` (the pair it never touches), and the whole call chain
that reaches it is gated on `DAT_00b36218==6` -- a per-player game-state
field ALREADY independently documented elsewhere in this repo
(`re_notes/iw5sp.md` line ~912) as meaning "ordinary live SP/Survival
gameplay." This is now the leading theory: real code, an explicit
computation (not an implicit consistency assumption), and a gating condition
that matches "IT HAPPENS ONLY IN LIVE GAMEPLAY" exactly, independently
confirmed rather than newly guessed. A new diagnostic log
(`[video-scale-diag]`) has been shipped (built, redeployed) that will show
directly, on the next play session, whether/how far the two pairs actually
diverge at runtime -- the single most decisive available check.

**Retracted theory/fix (kept for the record, DO NOT reapply):** `FUN_00683060`
does create `SAVED_SCREEN` from `DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` while the other
9 render targets scale from `DAT_021d2e00`/`DAT_021d2e04` (the pair
`Hook_FUN_00679010` already overrides) -- that part of the decompile is
correct and re-confirmed (`FUN_00683060` line ~35-47: `DAT_021d2e08`/`0c`,
masked/clamped, feed directly into the `CreateRenderTarget` call tagged
`R_RENDERTARGET_SAVED_SCREEN`). What was WRONG was the assumption that this
pair is merely SAVED_SCREEN's own private, independently-tier-clamped
render-target size (a "low-risk, non-gameplay-critical" screenshot/thumbnail
buffer, safe to override). **User correction, live, immediately after
deploy:** "erm well turns out what you just set was actually the genuine
window size (it should match native monitor / res set not the upscaled
resolution)." I.e. `DAT_021d2e08`/`0c` doubles as the real backbuffer/OS
window size -- SAVED_SCREEN is deliberately sized to NATIVE display
resolution, not the internal supersampled scene resolution, because it's a
UI-facing capture (almost certainly the pause-menu/loading-screen background
snapshot). Overriding it to the upscaled target would have tried to resize
the actual OS window to the supersampled resolution on every scaled frame --
a new, real, separate bug, not a fix. **Confirmed via `re_notes/iw5sp.md`
lines 3110-3116** this pair is exactly what the menu/UI system's own final
composite stage targets: itemDef/menuDef rects render to a fixed 1920x1080
logical canvas, then a separate uniform-upscale stage stretches that canvas
to the real device backbuffer size -- i.e. this field is load-bearing for
the UI layer specifically, and was never actually a safe target to
overwrite. Reverted in `Hook_FUN_00679010` (`analog_input_hooks.cpp`):
the real trampoline's own internal tier-clamp logic now runs completely
untouched, exactly like before this investigation started. Built clean (0
errors), redeployed.

**Consequence for the earlier "SAVED_SCREEN mismatch" theory itself**: still
plausible as a genuine contributing factor (9 render targets at true native
resolution vs. SAVED_SCREEN capped lower IS a real, confirmed size
inconsistency the engine's own code can reasonably assume never happens),
but the correct fix -- if this is even the actual crash mechanism, still
unconfirmed -- is NOT "make SAVED_SCREEN match the other 9" (that field has
its own real, separate consumer). Any future attempt needs to keep the
window-size field at native and find a different way to reconcile
SAVED_SCREEN's size with the scaled scene, or conclude the mismatch isn't
actually the crash's cause at all and look elsewhere. Re-investigation
needed from here; user has stated clearly they consider it "100% a scaling
issue" that "IW knew of this limit" and remains "determined to fix it."

**The real mechanism**: direct user isolation test (`InternalRenderScalePercent`
on / at 100% / off, motion blur left enabled throughout) found the crash
tracks that ONE setting precisely -- reproduces whenever it's active at ANY
value including 100%, never reproduces when off. Full decompile of
`FUN_00683060` (the real render-target orchestrator, issue #88's own original
subject) confirmed why: of the 10 real render targets it creates, 9 (
`RESOLVED_SCENE`, `FLOAT_Z`, `SSAO`, `SSAO_BLURRED`, `SSAO_FLOAT_Z`,
`POST_EFFECT_0/1`, `PINGPONG_0/1`) scale from `DAT_021d2e00`/`DAT_021d2e04`
(the pair issue #88's own hook, `Hook_FUN_00679010`, already overrides) --
but `SAVED_SCREEN` uses a completely separate pair, `DAT_021d2e08`/
`DAT_021d2e0c`, independently tier-clamped (discrete steps 1280/1600/1920,
capped well below a real 2560x1440+ display) and never touched by the hook.
Since this project's own prior research already confirmed the engine's real,
natural, always-tested internal render resolution is 1920x1080 even inside a
larger backbuffer, "100%" was never actually a no-op -- it pushes the 9
tracked render targets up to true native resolution while `SAVED_SCREEN`
silently stays capped at its own lower tier ceiling, a genuine size mismatch
across a set of render targets the engine's own code can reasonably assume
are always consistent. "Off" leaves everything at the engine's own natural,
already-consistent default -- no mismatch, matching the isolation test
exactly. This is very likely exactly what IW's own original tier-clamp cap
was protecting against.

**(Superseded -- see the retraction at the top of this entry.)** The
paragraph that stood here previously claimed a fix overriding
`DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` to match the scaled target; that was wrong and
has been reverted, not applied. Left as a pointer rather than deleted so a
future read of this section in order doesn't land on stale instructions.

Live-reported: the game exited cleanly mid-session -- no error dialog, not
paused, not in any menu -- and could not be reliably reproduced. User's own
direct theory: "something about above native is making the GC or the memory
allocation shit itself."

**Investigated properly rather than assumed wrong or right:**
- Checked Windows Event Log (`Get-WinEvent`, Application log, `Id=1000`) for
  the actual incident window -- **no new crash event at all**, despite ~75
  minutes since the last real one. Also checked for GPU driver TDR events
  (System log) -- none.
- Checked this project's own `proxy_d3d9.log` -- ends with a clean
  `"proxy_d3d9 detach"`, NOT a crash-flushed trace (`FlushLogOnCrash`,
  `dllmain.cpp`'s real vectored exception handler, would have caught and
  flushed a genuine AV at the exact fault point -- it never fired).
- Checked for a native game console/crash log (CoD titles sometimes write
  one) -- none exists for this build.
- **Conclusion from the absence of evidence**: no Windows-level crash (no
  `0xc0000005`, no WER dialog) and no genuine unhandled exception occurred --
  ruling out a code-level AV bug in this project's own hooks as the direct
  cause, despite the process genuinely terminating.

**Real root cause, confirmed via fresh decompile**: this same session's own
earlier RE work (issue #95's Round 3 investigation) had already found and
decompiled the engine's real render-target allocation functions
(`FUN_00682fa0`/`FUN_00682d70`/`FUN_00682e50`), each with a real error path on
allocation failure: `FUN_00425540(0, "Couldn't create a %i x %i render target
surface: %s\n", ...)`. Decompiled `FUN_00425540` itself this pass -- it is
genuinely the engine's real `Com_Error`-equivalent: real severity-code
handling (`param_1` == 4/5/6/7, matching classic id Tech `ERR_FATAL`/
`ERR_DROP`-style codes), and terminates in a real
`FID_conflict____longjmp_internal(_Buf, _Value)` call -- Ghidra itself flags
this "Subroutine does not return." A `longjmp` is a normal, valid C control-
flow mechanism, NOT an illegal memory access -- it produces no AV, no WER
event, and nothing for `FlushLogOnCrash`'s vectored exception handler to
catch, exactly matching every piece of absence-of-evidence above. This is the
engine's own CONTROLLED response to a real allocation failure (e.g.
`CreateRenderTarget`/`CreateTexture` returning `D3DERR_OUTOFVIDEOMEMORY`), not
a crash in the traditional sense -- it unwinds cleanly back to a top-level
handler and, depending on the real severity code, can result in a clean
process exit with no dialog at all -- exactly "the game literally exited."
**User's own framing (2026-08-26), and correct**: "my guess is its not a
crash at all but a graceful exit forced by some flag we trigger" -- this is
now independently confirmed, not just a guess: see the 2026-08-26 parallel
fork pass below, where fork 2 found every real call site into
`FUN_00425540` passes severity `0`, which that function routes with ZERO UI
dialog straight to `longjmp` -- a genuinely graceful, controlled exit.

**Correction (2026-08-26, fork 2 of the parallel pass below)**: the specific
functions named in this paragraph, `FUN_00682fa0`/`FUN_00682d70`/
`FUN_00682e50`, are NOT actually what creates the 9 scaled render targets --
fresh decompile of `FUN_00683060` shows those 9 go through a different
mechanism (`FUN_004d08f0`+`FUN_004b60a0`); the three functions named here
only fire once, for a narrow, separately-gated swap-chain surface. The
underlying MECHANISM described in this paragraph (a real, severity-gated
`Com_Error`/`longjmp` exit on allocation failure) is still correct and still
the best-supported explanation for "clean exit, no dialog" -- see fork 2's
own findings below for the function citations that are actually confirmed
reachable from this project's own override.

**Why now**: the live config at the time had FOUR VRAM-heavy features active
simultaneously -- `InternalRenderScalePercent=150` (quadratic VRAM cost, issue
#88), `FsrSharpenEnabled=1`, `MotionBlurEnabled=1`, and
`ForceAnisotropicFiltering=1` (16x). None of these individually is new or
newly risky (each confirmed working live on its own), but stacked together
they represent genuinely heavy combined GPU memory pressure -- consistent with
this project's own earlier finding (issue #92, the `ForceD3D9On12`
investigation) that stacking multiple large render-target-sized workloads on
top of a high `InternalRenderScalePercent` is a real, plausible way to
exhaust VRAM, independent of `ForceD3D9On12` itself (which was OFF here).

**SUPERSEDED, 2026-08-26, same day -- this issue's own original VRAM-exhaustion
conclusion was WRONG, corrected via real live evidence, not more static
theorizing.** The mitigation below was never actually tested against a fresh
crash before being written -- it was a reasonable-sounding inference from the
`Com_Error`/`longjmp` mechanism found via static RE, not confirmed live. Real
evidence (via the newly-built `memdiff.exe livedump` mode, `tools/memdiff/`,
capturing FULL, uncapped process memory snapshots automatically every 5s plus
on a keypress, live during actual stress-test play) directly contradicts it:
- **The Hunk allocator was essentially idle across TWO separate real
  crashes** -- one where it sat completely frozen (`lowMark=0.10MB`,
  `highTempMark=0.02MB` out of its 10MB budget) for a full 3 minutes right up
  to the crash, another where it was equally idle on a much faster (~15s)
  crash. Nowhere close to its cap either time.
- **Real (uncapped, after fixing `memdiff`'s own artificial 1536MB/region-256MB
  scan caps -- see that tool's own commit for why those existed and were
  removed) total memory did not climb toward any ceiling** -- one crash's
  final 10 seconds showed total memory **decreasing** slightly (1807.7MB ->
  1787.9MB), with the two largest region-size changes being SHRINKS, not
  growth. No runaway single-region growth, no exhaustion signature, in either
  captured crash.
- Available virtual address space (32-bit process, `LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE`
  confirmed already active) stayed with real headroom free in both cases, not
  approaching its ceiling.

Direct user pushback that redirected the investigation correctly: **"why does
it matter, this crash is part of the phased changes or stuff around them,
maybe our upscaler has a bug itself?"** -- pointing at this SESSION'S OWN new
code instead of the native engine turned out to be exactly right. See issue
#95's own Round 4 entry for the real root cause and fix: `FUN_00497210`
(Phase E's real engine hook target) can fire MULTIPLE TIMES in a single real
frame via its actual caller `FUN_00508970` (a recursive viewport-rectangle
splitter for splitscreen/PIP exclusion zones), and Phase E's motion-blur pass
had no guard against running more than once per frame -- a real, intermittent
state-corruption risk (only when an exclusion zone is actually active, which
is why this never reproduced consistently), not a native-engine memory issue
at all. The mitigation text below (lower `InternalRenderScalePercent`) is left
in place as a real, still-valid recommendation if VRAM pressure is ever a
genuine concern running all of RCAS/motion blur/forced aniso together, but it
was NOT the actual cause of the crashes this issue investigated.

## Parallel deep-RE pass, 2026-08-26: 4 forks, 3 live leads + Demonware ruled out

Direct user request: "launch 4 forks for deep analysis on the dumps and
ghidra re." Four independent, non-overlapping angles, each writing to its own
scratch file first (avoiding concurrent edits to this doc), consolidated here
by the parent session. **None of the 3 leads below is confirmed live yet** --
that is the actual next step, not more static work. User's own framing mid-
pass, and correct: "my guess is its not a crash at all but a graceful exit
forced by some flag we trigger" -- independently confirmed by fork 2 below
(every real failure call site passes severity 0, routed with zero UI dialog
straight to `longjmp`).

### Demonware / anti-tamper -- RULED OUT

Raised directly by the user mid-investigation: "shit i didnt think ab this,
what if this is demonware anttamper related." Checked directly rather than
assumed either way:
- Fresh `dumpbin /imports` on BOTH `iw5sp.exe` and `iw5mp.exe`: `ADVAPI32`,
  `binkw32`, `d3d9`, `GDI32`, `KERNEL32`, `mss32`, `POWRPROF`, `SHELL32`,
  `steam_api`, `USER32`, `WINMM`, `WS2_32` (+`ole32`/`DSOUND` depending on
  binary). No `demonware.dll`, no `EasyAntiCheat.dll`, no `BEClient*`,
  nothing kernel-driver-shaped, in either binary. Per the sibling NSP
  project's own netcode research, Demonware is reached purely as raw socket
  traffic (`WS2_32.dll`) the game's own code initiates -- a backend service,
  not a locally-running anti-tamper agent capable of inspecting this
  project's injected DLL or killing the process from inside.
- **Decisive evidence, already on record but never connected to this
  question until now**: every captured incident's `proxy_d3d9.log` ends with
  a clean `"proxy_d3d9 detach"` line, meaning `DllMain`'s `DLL_PROCESS_DETACH`
  genuinely ran. `TerminateProcess` -- how an external watchdog/anti-cheat
  would forcibly kill a flagged process -- does NOT invoke `DllMain` DETACH
  notifications at all (documented Win32 behavior). A forced external kill
  would leave no such line. A clean detach means the process exited through a
  normal path, exactly matching the `FUN_00425540`/`longjmp` engine-exit
  mechanism already established above.
- **Conclusion**: this is a controlled internal engine exit, not an external
  kill. If a future incident's log is ever missing the clean detach line,
  that would flip this conclusion and warrant revisiting -- not expected, but
  worth watching for.

### Fork 1 -- second real consumer of `DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` found (a viewport sub-rect, not just SAVED_SCREEN)

Full report: `fork1_second_consumer_hunt.md` (session scratchpad, not
committed to the repo -- summarized here in full).

`DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` -- the pair already confirmed above to be the
real window size, feeding SAVED_SCREEN, and confirmed unsafe to override --
has a SECOND real consumer, never connected to this issue before: a
per-frame 3D-scene viewport sub-rect (`DAT_02802f60+0x174c/+0x1750/+0x1754/
+0x1758`, absolute `0x028046AC/B0/B4/B8`), copied directly from that pair by
`FUN_00463820` and inline inside `FUN_00469350` (already-committed RE from an
earlier, unrelated pass, never previously connected to issue #96). A
separate, independent pass (issue #95's own Round 3) confirmed this same
sub-rect is what `FUN_004e5b30` (the per-frame viewport-rect compute
function) selects whenever a mode flag is NOT the "full-screen" value -- a
real, per-frame-relevant 3D scene viewport rect, not a screenshot buffer.

**Why this reproduces the exact isolation-test signature**: `DAT_021d2e00`/
`DAT_021d2e04` (feeds `RESOLVED_SCENE` + 8 other real render targets) is a
direct, unclamped copy of the engine's own "requested W/H" fields, which this
project's hook overrides to `nativeW/H * pct / 100` using the TRUE
monitor-native resolution as the base, whenever `InternalRenderScalePercent
> 0`. `DAT_021d2e08`/`DAT_021d2e0c` is computed by the same real function via
its own INDEPENDENT tier-clamp (discrete steps 1280/1600/1920) and is NOT
derived from the field the hook overrides -- so the override never reaches
it. Net effect: the viewport sub-rect stays pinned near ~1920x1080 regardless
of the setting's value, while the 9 render targets track true native the
instant the feature is active AT ALL -- including exactly 100%, since the
hook's native-size source is the true display resolution, not the engine's
own ~1080p-capped default. This is a genuine, first-principles size MISMATCH
tied to the setting being on, not to any specific percentage -- exactly the
isolation test's own signature.

**Why it would explain the crash's intermittency**: this sub-rect path is
plausibly driven by the same "an exclusion zone/sub-view is active" condition
(`FUN_00508970`, the recursive viewport-rectangle splitter) already confirmed
to drive the motion-blur multi-fire bug (issue #95's own Round 4, above).
That fix only guards this project's OWN motion-blur pass against firing more
than once per frame; it does nothing about, and cannot fix, the NATIVE
engine's own viewport/render-target size relationship during the same
sub-rect rendering. Not independently confirmed this pass that the two share
the same trigger condition -- inferred from behavioral similarity, flagged as
the top next-RE-step below.

**Secondary finding**: no hardcoded max-texture-dimension check exists
anywhere in `FUN_00683060`'s allocation chain (checked directly) -- every
target's W/H undergoes only a floor-clamp to 1 and an `& 0xffff` mask, no
comparison against any literal or device cap. Rules out "a hardcoded ceiling
silently rejects the request" specifically within this function -- consistent
with fork 2's own findings below, and with the already-collected memdiff
evidence (no VRAM/address-space growth toward any ceiling).

**Open discrepancy, not resolved this pass**: two different mode-flag
addresses are cited for the same "full-screen vs. sub-rect" decision in
`FUN_004e5b30`, from two different RE passes -- one citation elsewhere in
this file gives `DAT_02802f60+0x1720`; issue #95's own Round 3 text gives
`DAT_02802f60+0x1760`. These are NOT the same field. Needs a fresh decompile
of `FUN_004e5b30` to resolve before this moves from "strong lead" to
"confirmed" -- do not trust either prior citation without re-checking.

**If confirmed live, the fix direction is NOT another poke to
`DAT_021d2e08`/`0c`** (already proven unsafe -- it's the real window size) --
it's making this project's own render-scale hook keep `DAT_02802f60`'s
downstream sub-rect consistent with whatever `DAT_021d2e00`/`04` actually end
up being (e.g. patching `FUN_00463820`'s own copy to use the same scaled
source the 9 render targets use), or clamping/disabling
`InternalRenderScalePercent` automatically whenever an exclusion-zone render
path is active.

### Fork 2 -- render-target allocation failure path: doc correction + a real unclamped consumer found

Full report: `fork2_allocation_failure_path.md` (session scratchpad). See
also the inline correction added above, near the original "Real root cause"
paragraph.

**Correction to this issue's existing text**: `FUN_00682fa0`/`FUN_00682d70`/
`FUN_00682e50` (cited above as the render-target allocators) are NOT actually
what creates the 9 scaled render targets -- fresh decompile of `FUN_00683060`
shows all 9 go through `FUN_004d08f0`+`FUN_004b60a0` instead; the three
originally-cited functions only fire once, for a narrow, separately-gated
swap-chain surface.

**The real confirmed-reachable failure site**: `FUN_00682bc0`, the engine's
shared depth-stencil surface creator. Cached once, but sized to the FULL,
undivided `DAT_021d2e00` x `DAT_021d2e04` pair (the exact pair this project's
hook overrides) -- and this single depth-stencil backs up to 8 of the 9
render targets simultaneously. Genuinely unclamped `CreateDepthStencilSurface`
call, real `FUN_00425540` error path on failure.

**Per-target divisors confirmed**: the SSAO family renders at half-res,
POST_EFFECT/PINGPONG at quarter-res (both scaled down from the base pair) --
but the SHARED DEPTH-STENCIL is always full-res regardless of any of that,
meaning it's the single largest, least-divided VRAM consumer in the whole
chain, and the one most likely to be first to hit a real driver-level
rejection if one is ever going to happen.

**No hardcoded ceiling exists** on `DAT_021d2e00`/`04` anywhere in this chain
(only a floor clamp) -- the override flows completely unclamped into every
D3D call downstream. A real driver-level rejection (VRAM exhaustion, or
exceeding `D3DCAPS9.MaxTextureWidth`/`MaxTextureHeight`) is the only
mechanism that could reject it -- not an artificial engine-side gate.

**All 4 real failure-call-sites in this chain pass severity `0`** to
`FUN_00425540`, which handles severity 0 with ZERO UI dialog, straight to
`longjmp` -- directly confirms the "clean exit, no dialog" symptom matches
this mechanism exactly, and directly confirms the user's own "graceful exit
forced by some flag we trigger" framing (see the top of this section).

**Real gap found**: this project's own code already DECLARES
`D3DCAPS9.MaxTextureWidth`/`MaxTextureHeight` but never actually READS them
anywhere -- no live data exists on the real device's actual caps. **Cheapest,
most decisive next-session step**: extend the existing `GetDeviceCaps` call
to log these two fields once at `CreateDevice` time, then compare against the
actual scaled dimensions `InternalRenderScalePercent` requests at whatever
value reproduces the crash. This would directly confirm or rule out "exceeds
real device caps" without needing any more static RE.

**Not resolved this pass**: `FUN_004425f0`'s 4 sub-creator dispatch targets
(the color-texture path, as opposed to the depth-stencil path above) were not
decompiled -- unknown whether they have their own separate, similarly-
unclamped failure path.
